paper.abstract:
In this paper, we give complete classifications of the finite groups $G$ for which the constant Eilenberg--Mac Lane spectra $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ are Anderson self-dual up to a virtual representation shift, and we determine all such shifts. For both of these spectra, we determine the representation periodicity lattice for every finite group.
  As applications, we obtain $RO(G)$-graded universal coefficient theorems relating equivariant homology and cohomology, together with formulas for the Anderson duals of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$-modules. In the $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ self-dual cases, we identify the graded $\mathbb F_2$-linear dual of the coefficient ring $\pi_\star^G H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ with a representation shift of the ring as a module over itself. This gives perfect multiplication pairings and graded self-injectivity.
paper.title: On the Anderson Dual of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$

paper.abstract: We study $\mathbf{E}_n$-algebras with ramification in their $\pi_0$ and in particular show that the existence of ramification places strong limitations on their chromatic behavior. In particular, we show that $\pi_0$ of nonzero $K(1)$-local $\mathbf{E}_4$-$\mathrm{KU}$-algebras cannot have a map from the ring of integers in a ramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$, and we show that a $p$-complete $\mathbf{E}_2$-ring with a map from a perfectoid ring into its $\pi_0$ is an associative $\mathbf{Z}_p$-algebra.
paper.title: Ramification in $\mathbf{E}_{n}$-algebras

paper.abstract: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.
paper.title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories

paper.abstract: We define the higher Dehn invariant on the Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical variants of scissors congruence $K$-theory, and prove that it makes these spectra into comodules over the spectral Sah algebra. This allows us to make the first formulation of the conjecture that the higher volume and Dehn invariants are jointly injective.
paper.title: Higher Spherical Scissors Congruence II: Comodules

paper.abstract: We compare homological and homotopical epimorphisms of associative algebras in monoidal $\infty$-categories. Assume that geometric realizations and pushouts of associative algebras exist and that tensoring preserves geometric realizations. Then every homological epimorphism is homotopical. If, in addition, the ambient category is additive and tensoring preserves finite coproducts, the converse holds. This extends the result of Chuang and Lazarev for dg-algebras. In the symmetric monoidal setting, we discuss consequences for centers and commutative refinements, as well as applications to derived analytic geometry.
paper.title: Homological and homotopical epimorphisms in monoidal $\infty$-categories

paper.abstract: From the perspective of homological algebra, exact categories are interesting because they possess derived categories. Typically, an additive category admits many exact structures. If the original category is sufficiently nice (for example, quasi-abelian), a classification of exact structures can be given in terms of certain Serre subcategories in the category of contravariant functors. It turns out that the derived categories of different exact structures are functorially related. This work is concerned with sufficient conditions for the derived equivalence of different exact structures on certain categories.
paper.title: On derived equivalences of exact structures on the category of representations $k[x]/(x^n)$

paper.abstract: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets. As an application of this result, we construct a binormal, combinatorial, proto-abelian category of Kashiwara crystals associated to any root system. In the case that the proto-exact category is a category of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers, we show how to reconstruct our family via the language of algebraic geometry codes, in particular motivating an extension to arbitrary finite fields. We provide explicit computations of the dimension and minimum distance for select families of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers.
paper.title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories

paper.abstract: We recast the theory of power operations in chromatic height $1$ using higher semiadditivity. In particular, we show that if the height $1$ cyclotomic extension of a commutative algebra $R$ is Galois, then power operations on $R$-algebras are exactly $\delta$-ring operations. We also show that semiadditive power operations on chromatically localized algebraic $K$-theory agree with power operations defined using polynomial functoriality. As an application, we deduce that the map from the $K$-theory of a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear symmetric monoidal category to its $K(1)$-localization is a $\delta$-ring homomorphism on the level of underlying spaces. It is well known that operations on the $K$-theory of $\mathbb{Q}$-linear symmetric monoidal categories are $\lambda$-ring operations, and since $\delta$-rings are `$p$-typical' $\lambda$-rings, this is an instance of the redshift philosophy.
paper.title: Semiadditive Power Operations in Chromatic Height $1$

paper.abstract: For an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum $R$ of chromatic height $k$, the trace method and the chromatic redshift imply that $T^n$-fixed point of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $R$ has chromatic height at most $k+n$. In this paper, we compute these heights for $H\mathbb{F}_p$, $H\mathbb{Z}$ and the $p$-complete connective image-of-$J$ spectrum $j_p$ for all primes and $n\geq1$, which are exactly $n-1$, $n$ and $n+1$, respectively. Our method is based on properties of Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology over $\mathrm{MU}$.
paper.title: Some chromatic height computations for homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology

paper.abstract: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.
paper.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry

paper.abstract:
We demonstrate that higher categories with adjoints behave like homotopy types. By the homotopy hypothesis, homotopy types can be regarded as higher categories in which all cells are invertible. We show that replacing invertibility by the existence of higher adjoints still supports a homotopy theory that is at least as rich as classical homotopy theory.
  The basic invariants of this theory are the homotopy monoidal categories \[ \Pi_n(X,x)=\operatorname{Ho}\bigl(\Omega^n(X,x)\bigr) \] associated to a based $(\infty,\infty)$-category with adjoints $(X,x)$. These invariants are monoidal categories with duals and replace iterated loops with iterated endomorphisms. The classical homotopy groups of the classifying space are recovered as the isomorphism classes of objects in the groupoid completion. We prove a Whitehead theorem for homotopy monoidal categories and show that fibrations of higher categories give rise to long oriented exact sequences of homotopy monoidal categories.
  To develop homological algebra of higher categories with adjoints, we prove an equivalence between skeletal sequences of categorical spectra with adjoints and categorical chain complexes, extending a result outlined by Lurie in the proof of the cobordism hypothesis.
paper.title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories with adjoints

paper.abstract: There is a long tradition of constructing smooth projective varieties in positive characteristic with non-degenerate Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequences. In this paper, we show that for any $n\geq 1$ and any spot $(i, j)$ on the $E_n$-page, except for the cases where the differential is forced to be zero for trivial reasons, there exists a smooth projective variety whose Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence has a non-zero differential with source $E_n^{i, j}$. Our construction is inspired by constructions of nilmanifolds in complex geometry and can be regarded as a positive characteristic analogue.
paper.title: The Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence can be arbitrarily non-degenerate in positive characteristic

paper.abstract: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which every positive residue characteristic of $S$ is invertible. We prove that Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients is canonically equivalent to modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The comparison identifies the corresponding commutative coefficient algebras and is compatible with arbitrary pullback. The theorem applies to singular and nonreduced schemes, including mixed-characteristic bases, and requires no excellence or finite-type hypothesis. Its special cases include rational coefficients over arbitrary bases, arbitrary coefficients over $\mathbb Q$-schemes, and $\mathbb Z[1/p]$-algebra coefficients over $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-schemes. The proof establishes base change for finite-cycle spectra using permutation quotients, families of cycles, and arithmetic power homotopies, then passes to general bases by universal homeomorphism invariance and continuity.
paper.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere

paper.abstract: Generalizing known results for $G=C_2$ and constant $\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-coefficients, we show the $RO(G)$-graded Bredon cohomology of a point with constant $\underline{k}$-coefficients is self-injective whenever $G$ is a finite subgroup of $SO(3)$ and $k$ is a finite field. Self-injectivity holds more generally for the $RO(G)$-graded homotopy of the Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum associated to a $k$-linear commutative Green functor $M$, whenever the spectrum $HM$ is Anderson self-dual.
paper.title: $RO(G)$-graded cohomology of a point is self-injective

paper.abstract: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes. In addition, for every positive integer k, we also construct holomorphic N=1 VOAs of central charge c=12k with index 24/gcd(24,k) -- conjectured to be the minimum -- in a computer-aided search carried out by AI coding agents. We overcome the exponential-time barrier by using chains of smaller cells to build ternary codes, whose indices can then be evaluated via a transfer-matrix technique, and we use a symmetric orbifold construction to reduce the problem of k=12 and 24 to that of k=6. Along the way, we also establish several results on ternary codes and their indices. Using an observation relating codes and Landau-Ginzburg orbifold models, we argue that the non-chiral doubles of the ternary code VOAs can always be gapped supersymmetrically.
paper.title: Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index

paper.abstract: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.
paper.title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms

paper.abstract:
We generalize to the enriched setting the classical theorem of Freyd, that the free cocompletion ${\mathscr PA}$ of a category ${\mathscr A}$ is complete if and only if ${\mathscr A}$ is approximately complete.
  The work of Day and Lack, arXiv:math/0610439, has laid the foundations for such a generalization and has had multiple applications in homotopy theory and in category theory. Our result allows us to expand on some of these applications.
paper.title: On the enriched approximate completeness

paper.abstract: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.
paper.title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings

paper.abstract: We prove that Atiyah duality holds in the $\infty$-category of non-$\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectra over arbitrary derived schemes: every smooth projective scheme is dualizable with dual given by the Thom spectrum of its negative tangent bundle. The Gysin maps recently constructed by L. Tang are a key ingredient in the proof. We then present several applications. First, we study $\mathbb A^1$-colocalization, which transforms any module over the $\mathbb A^1$-invariant sphere into an $\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectrum without changing its values on smooth projective schemes. This can be applied to all known $p$-adic cohomology theories and gives a new elementary approach to "logarithmic" or "tame" cohomology theories; it recovers for instance the logarithmic crystalline cohomology of strict normal crossings compactifications over perfect fields and shows that the latter is independent of the choice of compactification. Second, we prove a motivic Landweber exact functor theorem, associating a motivic spectrum to any graded formal group law classified by a flat map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Using this theorem, we compute the ring of $\mathbb P^1$-stable cohomology operations on the algebraic K-theory of qcqs derived schemes, and we prove that rational motivic cohomology is an idempotent motivic spectrum.
reasons: abstract: moduli stack of formal groups
paper.title: Atiyah duality for motivic spectra

paper.abstract: We prove relative Langlands duality for $X = GL_{p+q}/(GL_p \times GL_q)$. These symmetric spaces arise in the setting of the linear period of Friedberg-Jacquet when $p=q$, and exhibit non-tempered behavior when $q>p+1$. Via the real-symmetric correspondence, we establish a derived Satake equivalence for the real group $G_{\mathbb R}=U(p,q)$, and use it to obtain a constructible realization of coherent sheaves on Kato's exotic nilpotent cones. Along the way, we describe the dual variety of $X$ in terms of the Whittaker cotangent bundle and regular centralizers, viewed as Coulomb branches.
paper.title: Relative Langlands duality for linear periods

paper.abstract: We study spectral sequences as an obstruction theory to deforming cohomology classes via the Rees construction. A filtered complex is interpreted as an equivariant family over the affine line, in which higher spectral sequence differentials arise as obstructions to lifting cohomology classes through infinitesimal neighborhoods of the special fibre. This leads to various geometric and module-theoretic degeneration criteria. We give various applications to $\mathrm{Ext}$ spectral sequences for complex Lagrangians and the formality results of Melani-Rubi\'o amongst others. For double complexes, we revisit the Khovanov-Qi decomposition on the Rees side and introduce a two-parameter Rees construction over the affine plane. The higher differentials of the two associated spectral sequences correspond to torsion modules supported on the thickened coordinate axes. We obtain degeneration criteria in terms of these modules and an intrinsic characterisation of the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma.
paper.title: Deformations of cohomology classes and spectral sequences

paper.abstract: A celebrated conjecture of Gromov states that for closed aspherical manifolds, the vanishing of simplicial volume implies the vanishing of the Euler characteristic. We prove Gromov's conjecture for closed convex projective manifolds and, more generally, for closed orientable smooth manifolds admitting an immersed straightening. Generalising the straightening of simplices in properly convex domains in real projective space, we introduce the notion of immersed straightening and prove that, for every integer $d\geq 1$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that every closed orientable smooth $d$-manifold $M$ admitting an immersed straightening satisfies $|\chi(M)|\le C_d||M||$.
paper.title: Angle cocycles, Euler characteristic, and simplicial volume of smooth manifolds

paper.abstract: On stacks there is a richer version of $\mathcal{D}$-modules---called $\textit{potent }\mathcal{D}\textit{-modules}$---which decompletes at equivariant parameters, in the same sense that genuine equivariant $K$-theory decompletes equivariant cohomology. In this paper, we prove a ``genuine'' version of Kashiwara's lemma for $\mathcal{D}$-modules. Namely, we show that for a broad class of geometric stacks $X$, if $Z \subset X$ is a closed substack, the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}}(Z)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $Z$ is equivalent under pushforward to the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}} _Z(X)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $X$ with support contained in $Z$.
paper.title: Kashiwara's Lemma for Potent D-modules

paper.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $n\geq 1$. We prove that the Tate-Frobenius of the $\operatorname{K}(n)$-local sphere induces an equivalence between $L_{n-1}L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y$ and $(L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y)^{t\Sigma_p} \cong (L_nY)^{t\Sigma_p}$ for any finite $p$-local type $n-1$ spectrum $Y$ with trivial $\Sigma_p$-action.
paper.title: Tate Frobenius and chromatic blueshift of finite spectra

paper.abstract: Every nonempty connected finite-dimensional CW topological semigroup admits a continuous associative multiplication on its universal cover that lifts the multiplication of the base. Such a multiplication is unique up to a deck transformation: in fact, any two associative lifts are conjugate whenever they exist. We show that the finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped in general: a connected, countable, infinite-dimensional CW topological semigroup is constructed for which continuous lifts of multiplication exist, but none is associative. The counterexample has nonabelian fundamental group isomorphic to Thompson's group $F$. Thus finite dimensionality is sufficient for associative lifting in the CW setting, whereas the unrestricted infinite-dimensional statement fails.
paper.title: Associative Lifts of CW Semigroups

paper.abstract: We study higher complements of pseudohyperplane arrangements and the specialization maps between them, induced by degenerations. We develop a presheaf formalism on oriented matroids and weak maps, which model degenerations. Our main constructions are the posets of weighted and weightwise topes, which provide functorial combinatorial models for higher complements and their specialization morphisms. Their presheaf structure yields a deletion-contraction homotopy pushout, from which we derive a uniform combinatorial proof of the integral cohomology presentation for all $n \geq 2$. This presentation is natural with respect to weak maps and identifies cohomology rings with higher Orlik-Solomon algebras extending the known formulas for linear arrangements to non-realizable oriented matroids. Finally, we equip Deligne groupoids with a presheaf structure and identify them functorially with the fundamental groupoids of the complexified complements.
paper.title: Presheaf structures governed by oriented matroids and pseudohyperplane arrangements

paper.abstract: We compute the Chern classes of irreducible representations for the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$. Utilizing these computations, we investigate whether every even-dimensional class in the integral group cohomology of these families can be realized as a Chern class of some complex representation. It turns out that this realizability question answers in the affirmative for the generalized quaternion groups. In contrast, it turns out that the answer for dihedral groups is erratic.
paper.title: Realizable Cohomology Classes of Dihedral and Generalized Quaternion Groups

paper.abstract:
Sierksma's conjecture asserts that every affine map $a\colon\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ has at least $((r-1)!)^d$ unordered Tverberg partitions into $r$ parts. Until now, lower bounds growing with $d$ were known only when $r$ is a prime power. As one of our main results we prove that for every integer $r\geq3$, every decomposition $r=kq+s$ into $q=p^\alpha$ a prime power, $k\geq1$ and $s\geq0$, and every affine map $a$, the number $\operatorname{Tv}(a)$ of unordered Tverberg partitions satisfies \[
  \operatorname{Tv}(a)\ \geq\ \frac{q}{r!}\,\Big(\frac{q}{\alpha+1}\Big)^{\big\lceil\frac{(r-1-2s)(d+1)}{2}\big\rceil}. \]
paper.title: The number of Tverberg partitions beyond prime powers

paper.abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the canonical map $E\Gamma\to\underline{E}\Gamma$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.
paper.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory

paper.abstract: The cyclic homology of a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded, smooth and proper $A_\infty$ category satisfying the Hodge-to-de-Rham degeneration property carries the structure of a polarized semi-infinite Hodge structure or the so-called EP-structure. Given two $A_\infty$ algebras $A$ and $B$ with the above conditions, we construct a K\"unneth map from the tensor product of their cyclic homologies to the cyclic homology of the $A_\infty$ tensor product $A\otimes_\infty B$ and show that it respects the EP-structures. As an application, we show that if $A$ and $B$ are equipped with weak Calabi-Yau structures, then $A\otimes_\infty B$ also inherits a weak Calabi-Yau structure. Also, we show that the K\"unneth quasi-isomorphism respects good splittings of the Hodge filtration on $A$ and $B$ compatible with the weak Calabi-Yau structure. Our explicit calculations rely on the combinatorial (tree) description of the tensor product of $A_\infty$ algebras developed in \cite{amorim2016tensor}.
paper.title: A K\"unneth theorem for the cyclic homology of A-infinity algebras

paper.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Z\'u\~niga, are given.
paper.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology

paper.abstract: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-\'etale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.
paper.title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves

paper.abstract:
The localizing/separating factorization, which is the analogue, for restriction categories, to the surjective/embedding factorization for topoi, is developed at both the mere restriction category and join restriction category level. The factorization system at both the ordinary and join level is approached using the notion of a density, which is a stable and universal suborder of the restriction order. The main technical results of the paper construct the join localization and establish its basic properties. 
  The paper gives several examples of localizations. In particular, examples of localization on commutative rigs are provided which give a way to construct categories of schemes. The Zariski spectrum and the Pierce spectrum are, in particular, developed.
paper.title: Localizing Restriction Categories

paper.abstract: Fundamental to the field of topological signal processing (TSP) is the \textit{persistence diagram} (PD), or barcode, of a signal, which gives noise-resistant measures of topologically significant features as distinct from noise. Existing literature proves that the total persistence computed from these diagrams is equal to the total variation, for certain continuous signals on compact domains. We provide a closed formula for this shared quantity, and generalize to all continuous and discrete functions on bounded domains, and to certain functions on non-compact 1D manifolds. Extending the identification of continuous and discrete persistence, we investigate the similarities of functions with the same PDs, and prove that, for any $n$, the persistence diagram can be calculated as a function of the sequence of critical values; we compute these formulas for $n \leq 6$. Finally, we examine which function transformations cause predictable changes in the PD of the transformed function, characterizing affine and linear transformations.
paper.title: Bridging persistence of discrete and continuous 1D maps: Total variation, permutation equivalence, and diagonal affine transformations

paper.abstract: In this paper, we relate the space of line segments induced by a Jordan curve in the plane to the space of line segments induced by the plane by embedding the M¨obius band associated with the curve into the family of toruses associated with the plane; we further demonstrate how the geometric ”square condition” of the curve translates into a topological property through this embedding.
paper.title: Inscribed Square Problem and an Embedding of M¨obius Band in a Family of Solid Toruses

paper.abstract: We study the negative gradient flow of analytic maps $f:X\to\R$ defined on compact analytic Riemannian manifolds without imposing any nondegeneracy or transversality assumptions. We construct tight isolating blocks around the connected components of the critical set $\Crit(f)$ and record only bounded-time contacts made after an orbit exits one block and before it makes landfall within the interior of another. These contacts assemble into a strict topological category $\cL$ -- called the landfall category -- whose classifying space $B\cL$ is shown to be simple homotopy equivalent to $X$ naturally over all down-sets of the flow partial order. The filtered homotopy type is independent of the isolating blocks. Passing to a finite subanalytic triangulation yields a flow-induced acyclic partial matching, and hence, an explicit finite chain complex generated by the non-exit simplices of the blocks which computes the homology of $X$. The finite model also computes the Morse--Conley spectral sequence over arbitrary coefficients; over a field, homological perturbation further produces a connection matrix whose entries are finite sums over descending contact itineraries.
paper.title: Landfall Geometry

paper.abstract:
Background: Clinical influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) has often been low over the past two decades, highlighting the need for preseason VE forecasting. Timely forecasts could help health authorities plan prevention strategies and allocate healthcare resources. However, preseason forecasting of clinical influenza VE remains relatively uncommon.
  Methods: We obtained hemagglutinin (HA) sequences from GISAID for U.S. specimens collected in August--September before each influenza season from 2010--2011 through 2024--2025. After quality screening, we compared each virus with the corresponding vaccine target strain for the same season and subtype or lineage using two mathematical distances based on amino acid patterns in the HA protein. We calculated mean distances for each season and subtype or lineage and paired them with published clinical VE estimates, yielding 26 observations across 13 seasons. Using a mathematical AI approach, we fitted linear regression models of VE against each distance and evaluated their predictive performance by forecasting later seasons using data from earlier seasons, with the historical mean VE for each subtype or lineage as a reference. We then applied the same approach to 87 HA sequences collected in August--September 2026 to forecast VE for the 2026--2027 season.
  Results: We generated component-specific forecasts of influenza VE for the upcoming 2026--2027 U.S. season. Both mathematical distances were negatively associated with historical VE, indicating that greater differences between circulating viruses and vaccine strains were associated with lower VE. The topological model forecast VE of 40.3%, 56.9%, and 47.1% against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria, respectively, whereas the geometric model forecast corresponding VE values of 34.0%, 56.8%, and 51.1%.
paper.title: Mathematical AI Predicts 40% and 57% Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against H1N1 and H3N2, Respectively, for the 2026--2027 U.S. Season

paper.abstract: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.
paper.title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group

paper.abstract: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation in which the image of every codimension one face is a subcomplex. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.
paper.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners

paper.abstract: Bradley and Vigneaux define a generalized distance on a finite prefix poset using next-token probabilities. They conjecture that its higher magnitude homology vanishes. Motivated by their expression of magnitude as a weighted sum of homological Euler characteristics, we verify this conjecture for their explicit complex, in which both endpoint faces are zero. For each finite length, the homology groups in degrees two and above are zero. The degree-one homology group is free abelian, with one generator for each positive-probability edge of that length. The proof constructs a contracting homotopy for each component whose endpoints have an interior prefix. This homotopy inserts the least interior prefix. Edge probabilities zero and one are both allowed.
paper.title: Vanishing of Higher Magnitude Homology for Finite Prefix Models

paper.abstract:
Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent
  data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an
  $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete
  innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context
  of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces.
  Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of
  Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and
  nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing
  a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves
  culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax
  descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which,
  informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a
  suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf
  space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again,
  this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a
  reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf
  objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.
paper.title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality

paper.abstract: Segal computed $\pi_0$ of the equivariant sphere spectrum as the Burnside ring by a Pontryagin-Thom construction, transversality, and marks. We carry out the same argument in the motivic setting over a field $k$: the Burnside ring is replaced by the Grothendieck ring $A^u(\Gamma_k)$ of finite \'etale $k$-schemes decorated with a unit, the marks by the Dress map $d(L,u)=\mathrm{tr}_{L/k}\langle u\rangle$ into $\mathrm{GW}(k)$, and a Pontryagin-Thom map $A^u(\Gamma_k)\to\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)$ is shown to be surjective with kernel $\ker(d)$. This gives $\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)\cong\mathrm{GW}(k)$ for infinite perfect fields of characteristic $\ne 2$ without Morel's computation. We then identify $\ker(d)$, by a reciprocity law on $\mathbb{P}^1$, as the group of principal quadratic divisors of rational functions, so that $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere is the unit-decorated Burnside ring of $\Gamma_k$ modulo principal quadratic divisors. The transversality step is proved by an elementary "re-topping" argument.
paper.title: Pontryagin-Thom, $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere, and principal quadratic divisors

paper.abstract: We define a moduli space of continuous maps from smooth hypersurfaces varying in an ample linear system. To study its topology, we construct a scanning map to an appropriate section space and investigate its effect on homology. Our main innovation is a general argument based on Goodwillie calculus and applicable to various moduli spaces of maps. Along the way, we compute the Goodwillie tower of the section space functor based at any retractive space.
paper.title: The moduli space of maps from hypersurfaces and its Goodwillie tower

paper.abstract: This paper studies doctrines in categorical logic and their relations to fragments of geometric logic. After a brief account of the historical context for the notion of doctrine in categorical logic, we propose our working definition. We then show that there is a Galois connection between the poset of doctrines and the poset of fragments of geometric logic as defined in the framework of Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi, recently developed by the first and third authors. Concretely, the connection is realised by a general construction of syntactic categories and classifying topoi which encompasses all well-known examples in categorical logic. This yields a mirror symmetry, between the algebraic world of doctrines and the geometric world of topoi: to provide evidence of this phenomenon, we prove a few symmetric results relating doctrines and logics by means of syntactic categories and classifying topoi. We conclude with a discussion on the theme of conceptual completeness.
paper.title: Logic vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry

paper.abstract: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $\pi_n\star\pi_m\cong\pi_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups. Under this identification, the symmetry interchanging the two factors acts on $\pi_{n+m}$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{nm}$.
paper.title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes

paper.abstract: Discrete homotopy theory is a combinatorial homotopy theory defined for discrete objects. Barcelo--Severs--White conjectured that the homotopy groups of complements of $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements are isomorphic to the discrete homotopy groups of graphs associated with the Coxeter complexes. We show that this correspondence fails in general by giving a counterexample in degree two for the $4$-parabolic subspace arrangement of type $A_5$.
paper.title: Discrete homotopy of graphs and $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements

paper.abstract: We define a Nielsen coincidence number for pairs of maps $(f,g)$ where $f$ is $n$-valued and $g$ is $m$-valued. The classical definition of the Nielsen number does not work in this setting, but we propose a theory where coincidence classes are allowed to overlap. We invoke a notion of multiplicity of a coincidence point, which indicates to how many classes it can belong, and we show that our Nielsen number is a homotopy-invariant lower bound for the number of coincidence points with multiplicity. We show a computational result in terms of single-valued lift factors, and using this, a Wecken property for self-maps of the circle.
paper.title: Nielsen coincidence theory for $(n,m)$-valued pairs

paper.abstract: We give a combinatorial proof that every simple convex $3$-polytope admits a small cover without using the Four Color Theorem. We also prove that the assertion that every simple plane triangulation admits a mod~$2$ characteristic function with at most five values is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem.
paper.title: Small covers and the Four Color Theorem

paper.abstract: We study spanning quadrangulations of even triangulations of real projective spaces, using the higher-dimensional notion of quadrangulation introduced by Kaiser and Stehl\'{\i}k. We prove that every even triangulation of $\RP^d$, where $d\ge 2$, admits a spanning bipartite quadrangulation. Moreover, such a triangulation admits a spanning non-bipartite quadrangulation if and only if it is not balanced; if it is balanced, every spanning quadrangulation is bipartite. Our proofs use coloring monodromy: its orbits yield bipartite quadrangulations, while a covering-space construction gives non-bipartite ones. %In dimension three, a bipartite quadrangulation can always be chosen to induce $K_{2,2}$ on each tetrahedron. More generally, we establish a sufficient condition for the existence of spanning bipartite quadrangulations on closed manifolds in terms of the monodromy action, and derive a consequence involving the fundamental group.
paper.title: Spanning bipartite quadrangulations in even triangulations of real projective spaces

paper.abstract: We disprove the two-bases conjecture of Chávez-Lomelí, Merino, Noble, and Ramírez-Ibañez (Conjecture 5.8 in *Some Inequalities for the Tutte Polynomial*), which asserts that \(\max\{T_M(2,0),T_M(0,2)\}\ge T_M(1,1)\) whenever a matroid contains two disjoint bases or its ground set is the union of two bases. We construct a connected, self-dual, rationally representable matroid \(M\) of rank \(32\) on \(64\) elements whose ground set is partitioned into two bases, but for which \[ T_M(2,0)=T_M(0,2)=263656235940864 <275621102802945=T_M(1,1). \] The construction extends to an explicit infinite family \(M_m\) of rank \(2m\) on \(4m\) elements such that \[ \frac{\max\{T_{M_m}(2,0),T_{M_m}(0,2)\}}{T_{M_m}(1,1)}\longrightarrow0. \] Consequently, the corresponding additive and multiplicative Merino–Welsh inequalities also fail under the two-bases hypothesis. We additionally construct a simple and cosimple matroid on \(60\) elements whose ground set is partitioned into two bases and for which \(T_M(2,0)<T_M(1,1)\). This disproves the simple-matroid, two-bases-covering formulation of Conjecture 4.2 of Merino, Ibañez, and Rodríguez; its dual disproves the corresponding cosimple-matroid, two-disjoint-bases formulation. The constructions and inequalities are established by explicit rank functions, exact Tutte-polynomial evaluations, and elementary coefficient estimates.
paper.title: Counterexamples to the Two-Bases Conjecture for the Tutte Polynomial

paper.abstract: For every integer \(k\ge 3\), we construct \(k\)-connected matroids representable over every infinite field, with girth \(k\), arbitrarily large cogirth, and Merino–Welsh quotient \[ \Phi(M)=\frac{T_M(1,1)^2}{T_M(2,0)T_M(0,2)} \] tending to infinity. In particular, this disproves **Conjecture 7.2 of Csikvári (2026)**, which asserts the multiplicative Merino–Welsh inequality for simple and cosimple matroids, and therefore also the stronger **Conjecture 7.3** therein, as observed by its author. Our examples are rank truncations of direct sums of \(k\)-element circuits. We give a 3-connected counterexample on 1011 elements of rank 433, certified by exact integer arithmetic, and a 6048-element counterexample admitting a proof without computation. Taking the direct sum of a counterexample with its dual also gives a negative answer to **Problem 4.3 of Beke, Csáji, Csikvári, and Pituk (2024)**: the original maximum and additive Merino–Welsh inequalities can fail for simple and cosimple matroids. The same construction disproves **Conjecture 2 of Knauer, Martínez-Sandoval, and Merino (2026)**: for every fixed \(g\ge 3\), \(\Phi\) is unbounded even among matroids having both girth and cogirth exactly \(g\). The dual direct-sum examples need not be connected; these constructions do not disprove the graphical or binary versions.
paper.title: Highly Connected Counterexamples to the Multiplicative Merino–Welsh Inequality

paper.abstract: We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory
paper.title: Rational analytic prismatization

paper.abstract:
We show that for almost every finite dimensional complex representation $W$ of $SO(2)$ the associated complex projective space $\mathbb{C}P(W)_+$ does not have the rational stable homotopy type of a specific wedge of representation spheres constructed from a chosen filtration of $\mathbb{C}P(W)_+$. This contrasts with the case for representations of finite Abelian groups where such an equivalence does hold.
  In the finite group case, the splitting result provides us with a classification result for projective spaces up to rational stable equivalence. In light of the non-splitting as a particular wedge of spheres in the case of projective spaces of $SO(2)$-representations, we also prove a separate classification theorem.
paper.title: Complex Projective Spaces in Rational $SO(2)$-Equivariant Stable Homotopy Theory

paper.abstract: We compute the $2$-completed integral motivic homology, effective algebraic $K$-theory, and very effective Hermitian $K$-theory of the geometric classifying spaces $B\mu_{2^n}$, $n\geq 2$, over algebraically closed and real closed fields. We first carry out the corresponding classical calculations and, then obtain the motivic results using motivic spectral sequences and comparison techniques. The results reveal the classical $2$-torsion together with motivic $\tau$-periodicity and $\rho$-torsion.
paper.title: On the Motivic K-Theories of Classifying Spaces of Cyclic 2-Groups

paper.abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.
paper.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four

paper.abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. Ekedahl proved an equivalence of triangulated categories between bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring and complexes of $F$-gauges. We give a geometric proof, independent of his proof, that the de Rham-Witt realization is a symmetric monoidal equivalence of stable $\infty$-categories between perfect $F$-gauges and bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring with Ekedahl's completed star product, as expected by Illusie. The geometry comes from topological restriction homology: $\mathrm{TR}^r(k;\mathbf Z_p)^{hS^1}$ is an iterated fibre product of copies of $\mathrm{TC}^-(k;\mathbf Z_p)$, and taking even stacks before and after the fibre product gives the genuine and the naive $r$-Nygaard stacks. Pushforward from the genuine to the naive $r$-Nygaard stack realizes Andriopoulos' $r$-Nygaard filtrations, which interpolate between the Nygaard filtration at $r=1$ and the Hodge-Witt filtration at $r=\infty$. On the genuine $r$-Nygaard stack, which is a chain of Nygaard charts, restriction and Frobenius come from the inclusions of sub-chains, Verschiebung from duality, and the differential as a Bockstein operator, and the relations of the star product become projection formulas. As applications, we deduce Ekedahl's K\"unneth formula and Poincar\'e duality for de Rham-Witt cohomology from their counterparts for $F$-gauge cohomology, and show that the special-value formulas of Illusie and of Mondal over finite fields are equivalent.
paper.title: The stacky approach to de Rham-Witt cohomology

paper.abstract: In this note, we elaborate on a result of Krannich--Kupers--Mehzer on Disc-presheaves. We show that equivalences of $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves of manifolds yields homotopy equivalences with trivial normal invariant. As an application, we show that two closed, simply connected manifolds are homeomorphic if and only if their $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves are equivalent.
paper.title: Disc-presheaves and normal invariants

paper.abstract: The classical Dold--Kan correspondence identifies simplicial modules with connective chain complexes. Using Morita theory, we construct a Dold--Kan-type correspondence for every linear category carrying a suitable action of the maximum-preserving simplicial operators. The construction functorially assigns a Morita-equivalent normalized category to every such linear category. In particular, we obtain Dold--Kan-type correspondences for all crossed simplicial groups. We prove a rank formula for the normalized hom-modules and show that a crossed simplicial group is self-dual precisely when its underlying simplicial set of automorphism groups has dimension one. Furthermore, we construct normalization-compatible self-dualities and recover the Dwyer--Kan correspondence for duplicial, paracyclic and N-cyclic modules.
paper.title: Dold--Kan Correspondences via Morita Normalization

paper.abstract: This book presents calculations of the $2$-primary components of the homotopy groups $\pi_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq 28$ and all $n$, as well as some $\pi_{29}(\mathit{SO}(n))$, with explicit generators.
paper.title: Homotopy Groups of Special Orthogonal Groups in Degrees 23 to 29

paper.abstract: The Euler characteristic transform (ECT) is a computable topological signature for shapes embedded in Euclidean space. Existing ECT stability results control changes in the transform through deterministic geometric perturbation bounds, but many data-generating mechanisms produce perturbations that are random and unbounded in the worst case. In such settings a uniform deterministic bound may be unavailable or too pessimistic. This paper formulates a probabilistic stability-transfer principle for one-dimensional ECT stability: a deterministic stability estimate is combined with a tail bound for the induced geometric error to obtain a high-probability ECT error bound. We instantiate this principle using the stability theorem of Marsh and Beers for embeddings of finite one-dimensional CW complexes. The resulting consequences cover ambient displacement fields conditionally on admissibility and supremum-tail estimates, and finite landmark perturbations with reconstruction. For landmark perturbations, bounded, sub-Gaussian, sub-exponential, and polynomial-tail noise assumptions give explicit high-probability ECT stability bounds. The framework isolates a geometric stochastic component that arises in shape analysis pipelines across biological morphology, medical imaging, molecular structure analysis, and remote sensing.
paper.title: Probabilistic Stability Transfer for One-Dimensional Euler Characteristic Transforms

paper.abstract: We construct a height-five prime ideal $P$ in the six-variable formal power series ring $R$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $P^{(2)}\not\subseteq\mathfrak{m}P$, thus providing a prime-ideal counterexample to the Eisenbud--Mazur conjecture (with $\mathbb{Q}$ being the coefficient field). The ideal is the kernel of an explicit quadratic parametrization over a number field of degree $28$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. A witness has order three, with leading term the determinant of a symmetric $3\times3$ matrix. We construct the witness by eliminating critical values to all orders and then straightening the resulting formal curve. Interpolation at the $28$ nodes of an arrangement of eight lines supplies the required lifting maps. A rational linear functional on third and fourth jets certifies nonmembership in $\mathfrak{m}P$. The construction also yields an unmixed radical ideal with $28$ smooth branches over $\mathbb{C}$, and provides a counterexample to the more general form of the Eisenbud--Mazur conjecture stated by More (with $\mathbb{C}$ being the coefficient field). Finally, the prime ideal counterexample descends to the localized polynomial ring $\mathbb{Q}[x_0,\ldots,x_5]_{(x_0,\ldots,x_5)}$, where a polynomial witness with the same fourth jet exists. All finite identities used in the proof admit exact verification.
paper.title: A counterexample to the Eisenbud–Mazur conjecture

paper.abstract: We exhibit the $p$-complete $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_p$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_p^{\wedge}$ as $\mathbb{E_3}$-$\mathrm{MGL}_p^{\wedge}$-motivic Thom spectra over the motivic $\mathbb{G}_m$-loop spaces $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BGL}$ and $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BSL}$, respectively. Furthermore, for $p=2$, we compute the $\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}$-relative $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology $\mathbb{G}_m \odot^{\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}} {-}$, recently introduced by Bachmann-Burklund-Dundas-{\O}stv{\ae}r, of $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$ to be $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{BGL}]$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}[\mathrm{BSL}]$ as $\mathbb{E}_2$-$\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$-algebras and $\mathbb{E}_2$-$(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$-algebras, respectively.
paper.title: $\mathbb{C}$-Motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane Spectra as $\mathrm{MGL}$-Motivic Thom Spectra and Normed $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology

paper.abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit Dennis trace maps from algebraic $K$-theory to Hochschild homology for dg module and curved dg comodule categories, and prove their compatibility with derived Koszul duality. For this, we construct a natural chain map $\tau$ from the chains on the newly defined thickened nerve to the total complex of the dg cyclic nerve, with explicit formulas incorporating morphisms and coherent higher homotopies, which generalizes McCarthy's approach. This $\tau$ construction works both for modules over dg algebras and for cdg comodules over counital conilpotent curved dg coalgebras. Combining the $\tau$ with the dg-enriched Waldhausen $S_\bullet$-construction and a Hochschild delooping theorem yields the Dennis trace maps. For thick subcategories corresponding under derived Koszul duality, we prove that the induced $K$-theory equivalences and Hochschild homology isomorphisms fit into natural commutative diagrams with these trace maps.
paper.title: An explicit Dennis trace and its compatibility with Koszul duality

paper.abstract: Motivated by the desire to turn the cobordism hypothesis (a statement about the universal property of some $n$-category of bordisms) into a $1$-categorical statement, we prove that all $n$-categories can be modeled by \emph{$n$-cospan contexts}: these are $1$-categories equipped with a collection of iterated cospans that satisfy a composition property in terms of pushouts. In particular, we construct an adjunction from $\mathsf{Cat}_n$ to the category of $n$-cospan contexts which simultaneously generalizes the $n$-fold span construction of Haugseng and the twisted arrow category construction (when $n = 1$).
paper.title: Cospan contexts and higher categories

paper.abstract: In general, it is interesting to investigate the complexity of simplicial maps under various topological constraints. In this paper, we consider maps between (triangulated oriented rational homology) manifolds with non-zero Hopf invariant and establish bounds on the simplicial complexity of the fiber of a regular point. The lower bound, which is cubic in the dimension, is proved via a refinement of a theorem of S. Eilenberg. The upper bound is notable in that it is uniform with respect to the Hopf invariant.
paper.title: On simplicial maps with non-zero Hopf invariant

paper.abstract: We refine the proper descent of Postnikov completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces to the dualizable world.
paper.title: Refined proper descent for left completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces

paper.abstract: We introduce the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings and begin the development of their theory over an arbitrary base scheme $S$, in analogy to that of higher coverings in an $\infty$-topos. We show that for $n=0$, our notion recovers Morel's $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings between simplicial sheaves. Under suitable assumptions, we then provide a Galois-theoretic classification of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings. Finally, we answer a question of Morel concerning a geometric criterion for $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings in the negative.
paper.title: On the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings

paper.abstract: Finite quasihamiltonian groups - that is, finite groups in which every pair of subgroups commutes - admit several characterizations. In this work, after introducing the notion of sectional contractibility graph, we provide a new characterization in terms of (a suitable subgroup of) magnitude homology. Our approach especially focuses on the subgroup lattices of finite groups and on the related notion of modularity. We present a detailed study for finite 2-groups, and, in particular, in the case of extraspecial 2-groups and Pauli groups. These groups, of interest because of their diverse applications in both mathematics and physics, already describe the wealth of information that one can obtain in restricting the study to the case of 2-groups.
paper.title: A characterization of finite modular 2-groups via magnitude homology

paper.abstract: In the paper \emph{Structure and realizability for rational maps}, Wei proved the following. Let \(k\) nontrivial partitions of an integer \(d\ge 3\) be given, satisfying the Riemann--Hurwitz formula for the case of maps between two spheres. If \(k>\ell+1\), where \[ \ell=\min_i|\pi_i| \] is the shortest partition length, then there exists a rational map whose branch datum is given by these partitions. In this paper we give a new proof of Wei's theorem on realizing a tuple of partitions as the ramification data of a rational function. The proof is inductive on the shortest partition length. Two auxiliary results are established: a two-cut partition theorem and a gluing theorem for marked spherical coverings. These reduce any counterexample with shortest length \(\ell\ge3\) to auxiliary data with either fewer factors or smaller shortest length, while preserving the total defect and the marked conditions. The base case \(\ell\le2\) is quoted from the literature.
paper.title: A New Proof of Wei's Theorem

paper.abstract: We give a direct Fox-calculus proof of the known rational asphericity theorem for every finite presentation complex with one nontrivial relator, including proper powers. The proof uses completed Fox derivatives and the absence of zero divisors in the completed algebra of a prounipotent group. Exact scalar extension to the finite adeles then yields adelic asphericity and a product decomposition of the higher homotopy groups of integral Bousfield--Kan completion. We also prove rational and pro-\(p\) analogues of Mannan's formula for finite two-complexes, with their natural topologies and fundamental group actions. The rational cohomological Whitehead criterion is proved directly. For a discrete one-relator group with relator not a proper power, we show that the tower \(L_2\nu_n(G)\) is Mittag--Leffler. Consequently \(\limone_nL_2\nu_n(G)=0\), and \(\pi_2(\Z_\infty BG)\) is naturally the inverse limit of the nilpotent Baer invariants. We identify this Baer limit canonically and topologically with the kernel of the integral augmentation-completed Fox operator and with the product of its local pro-\(p\) kernels. The comparison yields a torsion-free profinite homotopy module, vanishing inverse limits of the finite-stage transgression kernels, and explicit lifting obstructions. These results provide a homotopy-theoretic framework for the question of Serre in Gildenhuys's corrected formulation.
paper.title: Adelic Asphericity and One-Relator Pro-\(p\) Groups

paper.abstract:
The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory.
  The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.
paper.title: An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps

paper.abstract: Over every nonzero commutative ring $R$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose finitely generated thick subcategories are alegbraic, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.
paper.title: Finitely enhanced nontopological triangulated categories

paper.abstract: We determine the distribution of the homotopy type of the Vietoris-Rips complex of a fixed number of independent uniform points on a circle. An exact identity expresses each binomial moment of a periodic-orbit count as one probability for circular gaps, multiplied by a constant avoidance factor. We evaluate these probabilities by finite lattice-point counts and interpolation, obtaining explicit formulas for every sample size and every real scale. On an explicit rational partition, the probabilities are continuous piecewise polynomials of degree at most one less than the sample size. We also determine the homotopy distribution in the first transition window above each positive critical fraction $c_t=t/(2t+1)$. In this window the number of critical periodic orbits converges to a Poisson law with explicit intensity, yielding the limiting probabilities of the preceding odd sphere, the contractible type, and every wedge multiplicity of the critical even sphere.
paper.title: Homotopy distributions for Vietoris-Rips complexes of random circle samples

paper.abstract: We use Neumann's normal form to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree in either orientation, starting from the recognised Seifert or graph-manifold structure of the cover. For many non-alternating knots with at most thirteen crossings whose unknotting numbers were unknown, this identifies the cases in which the Heegaard Floer homology of the cover can be computed from such a plumbing, and shows for most of the others that it cannot. We determine 112 new unknotting numbers. For 43 of them, the lower bound rests on Heegaard Floer homology computed from the plumbing; for the other 69, it comes from linking pairings and from a theorem of McCoy and Park on special alternating knots. Finally, we show that the knot 13n1587 is a further explicit counterexample to the Bernhard--Jablan conjecture, after 13n3370.
paper.title: Negative-Definite Plumbings and New Unknotting Numbers

paper.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that every finite simplicial triangulation of real projective five-space has at least twenty-four vertices. Together with the construction of Guyer, Steinerberger, and Yang, this determines the minimum. A cup-product argument produces an induced subcomplex on sixteen or seventeen vertices. Transfer to the spherical double cover then imposes a covering condition on its lifted faces. In the sixteen-vertex case, a direct capacity bound excludes twenty-two vertices. For twenty-three vertices, a cochain extension argument reduces every relevant completion to one of 115 critical signed complexes; integer weights and exact covering certificates exclude all of them. The argument requires no assumption that the triangulation is combinatorial.
paper.title: The minimum number of vertices of a triangulation of $\mathbb{RP}^5$

paper.abstract:
We construct multiplicative norms on equivariant nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory for finite groups $G$. We also construct a genuine equivariant version of THH equipped with a Dennis trace map from K-theory compatible with the multiplicative norms. To do so, we follow the general strategy of Blumberg-Gepner-Tabuada in the nonequivariant case by generalizing their category of localizing motives to the genuine equivariant context, building upon the theory of perfect $G$-stable categories of the first-named author. Crucially, we proceed using the recent perspective on noncommutative motives by the second-named author with Sosnilo and Winges which allows us to deal with non-exact functors on this category of motives. Together with an isotropy separation argument for equivariant cubes, we prove our main theorem that norms of stable categories preserve equivariant motivic equivalences. As an immediate consequence, we obtain a unique equivariant multiplicative refinement of nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory.
  From these constructions and results, we draw several applications, namely: (1) that the endofunctor of (equivariant) tensor powers on ordinary perfect stable categories preserve motivic equivalences; (2) that the multiplicative norms also preserve the additive motivic equivalences, thus yielding a motivic refinement of a result of Elmanto-Haugseng and Cnossen-Haugseng-Lenz-Linskens that connective algebraic K-theory admits multiplicative norms; (3) we construct a genuine equivariant version of topological Hochschild homology equipped with a Dennis trace map that is compatible with multiplicative norms; and (4) we prove that every genuine $G$-spectrum is the K-theory of a perfect $G$-stable category.
paper.title: Equivariant localizing motives and multiplicative norms on algebraic K-theory

paper.abstract: We lay down the foundations of a theory of parametrised functor calculus, generalising parts of the functor calculus of Goodwillie. We introduce the notion of excisable posets and develop a theory of excisive approximations in this context. As an application, we introduce two different excisable posets when parametrising over an atomic orbital category. By comparing the notions of excisiveness for these two posets, we relate the invertibility of certain spheres with Nardin's notion of parametrised semiadditivity, generalising Wirthm\"uller's classical result in equivariant homotopy theory for finite groups.
paper.title: Parametrised functor calculus: excision, spheres, and semiadditivity

paper.abstract: Let $\mathrm{DY} = \mathbb{1}/(\eta, \nu) \in \mathrm{SH}(\mathbb{C})$. We construct a $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1 $w:\Sigma^{5,3}\mathrm{DY} \to \mathrm{DY}.$ The cofiber is a realization of $DA(1)$, the double of the subalgebra $A(1)$ of the $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Steenrod algebra $A$.
paper.title: A $\mathbb{C}$-motivic $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1

paper.abstract: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.
paper.title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs

paper.abstract:
We explore the analogy between rational G-spectra for an r-torus G and sheaves over an r-dimensional scheme, in the context of the author's algebraic model for rational G-spectra. In particular, the resolution of the sphere of a virtual representation in the standard model corresponds precisely to the Cousin complex resolution of a line bundle.
  The tom Dieck splitting for the sphere of an actual respresentation corresponds to the collapse of the Cousin spectral sequence by degrees, and the the non collapse in other cases corresponds to familiar geometric behaviour.
paper.title: Rational torus equivariant spectra VII: the Cousin complex

paper.abstract: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $\kappa$ for which they are $\kappa$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.
paper.title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings

paper.abstract: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.
paper.title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds

paper.abstract: We define an additive functor S that assigns a three parameter persistence module to every morphism between one parameter persistence modules. We show that if the morphism is bar-to-bar, then its image under S is rectangle decomposable. We prove that S is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and study further properties of the functor related to rectangle decompositions.
paper.title: A stable multipersistence invariant for ladder modules

paper.abstract: We study the facial structure of simplicial distribution polytopes using topological and algebraic methods. In the theory of simplicial distributions, measurement and event spaces are represented by simplicial sets, and compatible probability assignments form a convex polytope. Given a simplicial distribution, it is known that its supports determine its carrier face. Moreover, the supports form a simplicial subset of the event space. This naturally raises the question of how the topology of this simplicial subset is related to the corresponding carrier face. Our main objective is to relate the dimension of the carrier face to the topology and combinatorial structure of the space of supports. For $n$-facet-paired measurement spaces, we first express the carrier dimension in terms of the nullity of an associated facet matrix. When the measurement space is additionally orientable, we show that the carrier dimension is determined by the top-dimensional homology of the space of supports, yielding, in particular, a homological criterion for detecting vertices. We then develop an algebraic reduction based on a strong connectivity relation on the generating simplices of the space of supports. This construction yields a reduced facet matrix, indexed by the strongly connected components, whose null space is isomorphic to that of the original facet matrix. As a consequence, both the carrier dimension and extremality can be determined from the topology of the support and the way its strongly connected components are glued together.
paper.title: Homology and carrier faces of simplicial distributions

paper.abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.
paper.title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras

paper.abstract: We study versions of binomial and multichoose coefficients for finite $G$-sets, extending a result of Siebeneicher from the 1970s concerning the duality between these operations. If the group $G$ comes from a finite Galois extension of fields, the Dress map provides a bridge from $G$-sets to quadratic forms over the base field. We show that this Dress map is compatible with binomial coefficients of finite $G$-sets and a particular operation on quadratic forms we define. This allows us to extend the definition of Brugall\'e and Wickelgren's quadratically enriched binomial coefficients to arbitrary Grothendieck--Witt classes. This allows for a new proof that quadratically enriched binomial coefficients depend only on the trace form of the inputted \'etale algebra, as well as an elegant reproof of a result of Chen and Wickelgren about binomial coefficients over finite fields.
paper.title: Operations on $G$-sets and the Dress map

paper.abstract: We show that the Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for all primes p >= 11. This improves on the recently announced result by OpenAI that V(4) exists at the prime 1009.
paper.title: The Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for p >= 11

paper.abstract: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.
paper.title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap

paper.abstract: We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(\chi(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\). By gluing two blocks formed by \(G_2/SU(3)\cong S^6\) and the unit disk $D(V)$ of 12- dimensional real $S^1$-representation $V$ along their equivariantly identified free boundaries, we explicitly construct such a manifold $M^{18}_3$. We also prove that the four-point case is null-bordant in real dimension \(16\) and in every real dimension greater than \(18\); hence \(18\) is the smallest dimension in which such a counterexample occurs.
paper.title: Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture

paper.abstract: The obstruction to an effective $p$-adic manifold action is an integer signature tail. On asymptotically controlled rational modules over one fixed free $C_p$-space, finite-cover Mayer--Vietoris makes the difference between $p$ copies and quotient-permutation tensoring nilpotent. Every degree-four class therefore has eventually $p$-divisible signatures. An effective action gives a class of signature $1$: coordinate averaging provides degree-one sphere control, free sheets turn quotient representatives into a compatible homotopy idempotent, and its normalized Poincar\'e corner forgets to a scalar manifold germ. Successive localization boundaries recover one copy of $\CP^2$, up to sign. The resulting contradiction proves the Hilbert--Smith conjecture.
paper.title: Integral tail signatures and the Hilbert--Smith conjecture

paper.abstract: It is well known that the $[0,1]$ and $[0,2]$ Postnikov truncations of the units of the topological $K$-theories $\glone \KO$ and $\glone \KU$, respectively, are split, and that the splitting is provided by the ($\Z/2$-graded) line bundles. In this paper we give a similar splitting for the $[0,1]$-truncation of the units of algebraic $K$-theory, considered as a sheaf on affine schemes. A crucial step is to produce the splitting for $\glone K(\Z)$. Along the way we also give a complete calculation of the connective spectrum of strict units of $K(\Z)$ and $K(\F_\ell)$ for a prime $\ell$. Finally, we show that the units of algebraic $K$-theory do not split as a presheaf. In fact we show they do not even split pointwise.
paper.title: The spectrum of units of algebraic $K$-theory

paper.abstract:
