We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd,
  \qquad
  \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[
  \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!,
  \qquad
  \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.
paper.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality

paper.abstract: We establish a global equivariant refinement of the theorem of Snaith that presents the complex $K$-theory spectrum as a localization of the suspension spectrum of $\mathbb C P^\infty$. We prove that the morphism of ultra-commutative global ring spectra from $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$ that classifies the tautological $U(1)$-representation exhibits the global $K$-theory spectrum as a specific localization, in both the $\infty$-categories of ultra-commutative ring spectra and of commutative global ring spectra. The classes to be inverted are certain representation-graded $U(n)$-equivariant homotopy classes of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$, the pre-Bott classes. We also show that for every compact Lie group $G$, the $G$-equivariant $K$-theory spectrum is a telescopic localization of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_G U(1)$ by the pre-Bott classes of all unitary $G$-representations.
paper.title: Equivariant $K$-theory as a global localization

paper.abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.
paper.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic

paper.abstract: Deformation theory studies how varieties and other algebro-geometric objects vary in families. A central part of the subject is formal deformation theory, where one deforms over an Artinian base; such deformation problems are governed by Lie algebraic models. We pose the question of deforming varieties over nilpotent but not necessarily Artinian bases. These turn out to be classified by the same Lie algebraic models plus some topological structure. More precisely, we will consider partition Lie algebroids in the category of ultrasolid modules, a variation of the solid modules of Clausen and Scholze that give a well-behaved category akin to topological modules. To approach this result, we decompose deformation problems into n-nilpotent layers. Each of these layers is individually easier to understand, and is classified by simpler variants of partition Lie algebras.
paper.title: Nilpotent Deformation Theory via Ultrasolid Algebra

paper.abstract: We introduce and develop the theory of distributivity for base categories equipped with so-called atomic orbital subcategories, with an eye towards applications in equivariant homotopy theory. This extends the important framework in Nardin's thesis and supplies several crucial details on distributivity missing from the treatment therein. As our main technical result, we provide a parametrised distributive version of the universal property of "partial cocompletions with relations". We then employ this to construct a distributively normed symmetric monoidal structure on presentable categories. In turn, by specialising to the case of equivariant homotopy theory for compact Lie groups G, we show that the category of genuine G-spectra is normed idempotent, so that we obtain the structure of multiplicative norms on G-spectra along inclusions of finite index subgroups.
paper.title: Normed idempotence of spectra and distributivity in equivariant higher algebra

paper.abstract: For any non-zero $\mathbb{E}_4$-ring $R$, we prove that an $n$-fold direct sum of suspensions of $R$ cannot admit an exhaustive filtration by fewer than $n$ cells. We do this by showing that certain integral representations of the symmetric group lift to Schur functors on additively $\mathbb{E}_3$-monoidal $\infty$-categories. We then reduce the statement to a vanishing fact for rational Schur functors due to Deligne.
paper.title: The invariant cell number property for $\mathbb{E}_4$-rings

paper.abstract: We construct simply connected, closed smooth manifolds whose rational homotopy types are elliptic and whose homology nilpotency exceeds rational category by arbitrarily large amounts. This separates short models from short quotients of minimal models. The construction starts from an explicit family of minimal Sullivan algebras with finite-dimensional cohomology. A finite quotient establishes Poincar\'e duality and gives an upper bound for homology nilpotency, while a closed orientation functional computes rational category. Two forced primitives yield the lower bound. An even regrading separates the relevant weights, extending this obstruction to every graded acyclic differential ideal. Rational surgery realizes the resulting models in their formal dimensions, with vanishing rational Pontryagin classes and arbitrarily large rational connectivity. The ratio of homology nilpotency to rational category tends to four thirds. Finally, under an external spherical stabilization statement, attaching a single cone can increase homology nilpotency by an arbitrarily large amount while leaving rational category unchanged.
paper.title: Unbounded Nilpotency Gaps on Rationally Elliptic Manifolds

paper.abstract: Real Betti realization is a symmetric monoidal functor from the category of motivic spectra to that of topological spectra, extending the functor that associates to a scheme over $\mathbb{R}$ the space of its real points. In this article, we identify the $\mathcal{E}_1$-ring structure on the real realization of $\mathsf{ko}$, the very effective cover of Hermitian K-theory $\mathsf{KO}$, by an explicit 2-local fracture square, as being equivalent to $\mathsf{L}(\mathbb{R})_{\geq 0}$, the connective L-theory spectrum of $\mathbb{R}$. Along the way, we also compute the real realization of other motivic ring spectra: motivic cohomology $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}/2$, the variant $\widetilde{\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$, $\mathsf{KO}$, the very effective cover $\mathsf{kgl}$ of algebraic K-theory $\mathsf{KGL}$.
paper.title: The real Betti realization of very effective Hermitian K-theory

paper.abstract: We resolve a conjecture of S. Plotnick from 1983 concerning the homotopy type of four-dimensional knot complements. We show that the exteriors of two branched twist spins of the trefoil, which were shown by Plotnick not to be homotopy equivalent as boundary pairs and hence not homeomorphic, are in fact simple homotopy equivalent. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of an explicit element of augmentation $49$ in the integral group ring of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5)$ which is a unit modulo the group norm and commutes with the element inducing the monodromy on the fundamental group.
paper.title: A counterexample to a conjecture of Plotnick on knot exteriors

paper.abstract: Global transfer systems are combinatorial objects that parametrize intermediate levels of structures and properties in globally equivariant homotopy theory. In this paper we study the lattice of global transfer systems, expanding beyond the case of abelian groups which was computed by the second author. The main result is a proof that the irreducible elements of the lattice of global transfer systems are strictly controlled by subgroups of groups which we refer to as endopure. From the irreducible elements one can recover the whole lattice, and studying these endopure subgroups leads us to a wide range of new phenomena and computations.
paper.title: Global transfer systems and endopurity of subgroups

paper.abstract: Bouc's hook cycles span the rational top homology of the matching complex of $K_{2k+1}$. We prove that their integral saturation quotient has exponent exactly $2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$ for every $k\geq1$, and construct divided-power cycles attaining this bound. For $k\geq2$, the homology lattice is not isomorphic to the standard integral hook lattice as an $\mathfrak S_{2k+1}$-module. For circulant complexes, we determine the integral dihedral homology modules of $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s}^{s-1})$, $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+1}^{s-1})$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+2}^{s-1})$, for $s\geq3$, $s\geq2$ and $s\geq3$, respectively, and classify the least scalar lifts of all primitive equivariant quotients to the rank-one module with trivial rotation and negative reflection. Tate localization relates prime-order gluing to fixed-point homology under a free, single-degree homology hypothesis. Explicit cycle subgroups separate saturation defects from obstructions to equivariant sections. For circulant independence complexes with jumps two and three, we prove an eight-periodic ordinary homotopy classification and a fixed-space obstruction to uniform representation suspensions. For every fixed nonempty bounded positive jump set, a finite-state construction gives a rational critical-face series.
paper.title: Integral homology lattices of matching and circulant complexes

paper.abstract: We give homotopy-theoretic proofs of the principal results of non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery. These include the Fundamental Theorem of Poincar\'e surgery, the Poincar\'e transversality exact sequence, and the construction of Poincar\'e handle structures. All results apply in dimensions~$\ge 8$.
paper.title: Non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery

paper.abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg homology groups to group cohomology groups.
paper.title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces

paper.abstract: Let $T=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}=1\rangle$ be a generalised triangle group in which $W$ is the Farey word of a rational slope $q=r/s$, and suppose that $T$ is the fundamental group of a hyperbolic $3$-orbifold whose singular locus has no spherical vertices. Let $G=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}\rangle$ be the associated central extension. We compute an explicit free resolution of the trivial module over $\mathbb{Z}G$ of minimal length, with differentials given in closed form by Fox derivatives. From this resolution we deduce an explicit free resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ which is $2$-periodic in degrees at least two, and we compute the integral homology and cohomology of both groups. Strebel treated the classical family $q=0/1$ in 1983. Since then only the family $q=1/2$ has been treated, by Ellis and Williams, and for that family our resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ has strictly smaller rank in every degree.
paper.title: Resolutions of orbifold generalised triangle groups

paper.abstract: We determine the $RO(C_2)$-graded $k\mathbb R$-Hurewicz image, where $k \mathbb R$ denotes the connective Atiyah's Real $K$-theory spectrum. As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families in the $RO(C_2)$-graded equivariant stable stems that are $C_2$-equivariant refinements of the classical $\mu$-families. Using a $C_2$-equivariant $v_{1,0}$-self map, we explicitly construct an equivariant Adams periodicity operator $P_{C_2}$ that captures these $v_1$-periodicity phenomena in the $C_2$-stable stems.
paper.title: The $RO(C_2)$-graded Hurewicz image of Atiyah's Real K-theory

paper.abstract: We study the category of constructible $p$-Kummer-\'{e}tale sheaves on the log adic generic fiber $(\mathrm{X},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{D}})_\eta$ for the stratification induced by a horizontal normal crossings divisor $\mathrm{D}$, showing that it is antiequivalent to a category of finitely generated unit Laurent crystals on the log prismatic site. We give a local description of finitely generated unit crystals on a framed log affine in terms of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules, and show pushforward compatibility for strict log smooth proper morphisms.
paper.title: A prismatic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence

paper.abstract: The category of all topological spaces and homotopy classes of maps is cartesian closed. In fact, the $(\infty, 1)$-category of all topological spaces and continuous maps, localised at homotopy equivalences, is cartesian closed. We model the exponential object using a topological space whose points are continuous maps equipped with putative neighbourhood filters. In general, this topological space will not even be $T_1$-separated, but the evaluation map induces a natural weak homotopy equivalence witnessing the universal property.
paper.title: The classical homotopy category is cartesian closed

paper.abstract: We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $\Sigma$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $\Sigma$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes. Moreover, we provide examples showing the impossibility of locally approximating minimizing cycles by smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifolds, even in homology classes with smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth representatives.
paper.title: $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth approximation of mod $k$ integral cycles

paper.abstract: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.
paper.title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction

paper.abstract: This paper addresses the computation of persistent homology for filtrations of cellular cosheaves over a fixed cell complex, where the algebraic data vary along the filtration while the underlying topological structure remains unchanged. We extend methods from discrete Morse theory to this setting, establishing conditions under which chain complexes can be reduced while preserving the associated persistence module. Building on these results, we introduce "FilteredScythe", an algorithm that identifies Morse matchings compatible with all stages of the filtration and performs reductions using Schur complements, based on the exist "Scythe" algorithm. We prove the correctness of these reductions and establish bounds on the algorithm's time and space complexity.
paper.title: Discrete Morse Theory for Computing Filtered Cosheaf Homology

paper.abstract: This is my written Laudatio for Graeme Segal on receiving the Chern Medal at the 2026 International Congress of Mathematicians. I make some general remarks about Segal's qualities as a mathematician. Then I discuss the origins of his work on classifying spaces of categories and Gamma-spaces. In the last section I describe his axiom system for Wick-rotated quantum field theory and some of his subsequent work in the area. Of course, this is necessarily only a small slice of Segal's total research output.
paper.title: On the work of Graeme Segal

paper.abstract: We show that every vineyard can be decomposed into vines, that is, every path in the space of persistence diagrams $\mathcal{D}$ can be decomposed into a sequence of paths in $\mathbb R^2$. Moreover, we characterize which spaces $X$ have the property that every continuous map $X\to \mathcal{D}$ has such a decomposition. Our results hold not just for $\mathcal{D}$, but also for many other spaces of unordered tuples.
paper.title: Real Tree Vineyards have Vines

paper.abstract:
We prove that no nontrivial finite group $G$ satisfies the equivariant generating hypothesis of Bohmann, even when all $RO(H)$-graded homotopy groups are tested for every subgroup $H\leq G$. For each $G$, we construct ghosts on finite $G$-spectra with arbitrarily long nonzero composition powers. We also prove that the homotopy-module functors are nonfull and construct non-equivalent finite $G$-spectra with isomorphic full homotopy modules.
  A central ingredient of our proof is the natural ghost operation $\Psi=(p-[C_p/e])(1-g)$ on $C_p$-spectra. Motivated by Ma--Xu's examples in the motivic settings, we apply this operation to both a two-cell complex and products of complex projective spaces with cyclic permutation action, which produces arbitrarily long nonzero ghost powers. We also construct a ghost on an explicit four-cell complex that is detected in the derived category over the group ring.
paper.title: Equivariant generating hypotheses for finite groups

paper.abstract: We prove an unstraightening result for lax transformations between functors from an arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-category to that of $(\infty,2)$-categories. We apply this to study partially (op)lax and weighted (co)limits, giving fibrational descriptions of such (co)limits for diagrams valued in $(\infty,2)$-categories, to characterize adjoints in $(\infty,2)$-categories of functors and (op)lax transformations, and to prove a mate correspondence between lax transformations that are componentwise right adjoints and oplax transformations that are componentwise left adjoints, for such transformations among functors between arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-categories.
paper.title: Straightening for lax transformations and adjunctions of $(\infty,2)$-categories

paper.abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.
paper.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects

paper.abstract:
Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[
  I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$.
  We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.
paper.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space

paper.abstract: We identify the $(\infty,1)$-category presented by the dagger Bergner, dagger Joyal, and dagger Rezk models of Parts I and II with that of univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories. We first construct a realization--nerve adjunction between reversal simplicial anima and Hermitian flags. We prove that its nerve restricts to an equivalence between flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and dagger Segal anima, under which univalence corresponds to unitary completeness. We then construct the adjunctions for univalentization and Hermitian completion and identify univalentization with unitary completion.
paper.title: Models for dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories III: Univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and unitarily complete dagger Segal anima

paper.abstract: We propose a of definition conjugate stack for a class of suitable $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-algebras that includes the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle$ for all heights $n$. Then we calculate part of $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle^{\mathrm{conj}}$ as a quotient stack in terms of Witt vectors. To perform this computation we study generalized Thom spectra and their relative Topological Hochschild Homology. We exhibit the Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectrum $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{F}_2$ as a $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectrum, the $p$-local Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ (except for $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/4$) and $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ as $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}_{(p)}$-Thom spectra, and the connective complex K-theory spectrum $ku$ as $\mathbb{E}_1$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectra. We accompany these ``go" results with ``no-go" results that show these ``go" results do not admit $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-refinements.
paper.title: Generalized Thom Spectra, Conjugate Stacks, and truncated Brown-Peterson Spectra

paper.abstract: We investigate Eduard Hanslicks formalist aesthetics through the prism of Category Theory
paper.title: Hanslick's Musical Formalism as a Mathematical Structure - Examining meaning in Music through the Lens of Category Theory

paper.abstract:
We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic.
  The proof that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial uses the rational models for the Becker--Gottlieb and THH transfers obtained in previous work of the authors. In the appendix, we provide a second, more involved, proof that relies on constructing explicit $C_\infty$-algebra models for odd spherical fibrations (including circle bundles), which might be of independent interest.
  Concurrently, another counterexample (of very different flavor) was found by Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, and the first author.
paper.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras

paper.abstract: We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$. The original proof used the amenability of the images of sufficiently small local fundamental groups. Since that work was written, Kapovitch and Wilking proved Gromov's generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Their theorem gives the stronger conclusion that these local groups are uniformly virtually nilpotent. We explain how their result supplies a direct modern input for the bounded Betti number theorem. We also discuss the topological meaning of the bounded part of ordinary cohomology and its relation to the $\ell^1$-seminorm on homology.
paper.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers

paper.abstract: Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator. This relation is precisely the condition for cyclic compatibility on the associativity morphism, giving a new proof that $\mathsf{GRT}_1$ acts by cyclic automorphisms of parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams.
paper.title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group

paper.abstract: Persistent homology summarizes the topological evolution of a graph as persistence diagrams (PDs). Generating graphs whose topology matches a target descriptor is increasingly important, yet existing topology-aware generative models rely on soft regularization, producing graphs whose PDs may only be approximately similar. We initiate a principled investigation of the generation problem: produce graphs that realize a target PD exactly. We propose two approaches guided by the implicit local and global constraints a target PD imposes. The local approach builds degree-based PD-equivalent graphs iteratively, and we prove that every output realizes the target PD and that every degree-based PD-equivalent graph is reachable. However, as shown thereafter, local generation necessarily trades off between sample diversity and reaching infeasible states. We therefore recast generation as a global constraint satisfaction problem with a complete encoding solvable by modern constraint programming solvers. This is applicable to any vertex-based permutation equivariant filtration scheme and is minimal under the degree filtration. Experiments on four standard graph generation benchmarks confirm that both methods realize the target PD exactly. Together, our methods provide a principled treatment of strict topology-compliant graph generation. Code is available at https://github.com/Aalto-QuML/ExactCompliance.
paper.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs

paper.abstract:
We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions.
  Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.
paper.title: Groups with the fixed-point property

paper.abstract: We show by explicit counterexample that the Becker--Gottlieb transfer cannot be made functorial. A different counterexample using rational homotopy theory was discovered concurrently by the third author and Robin Stoll.
paper.title: The Becker--Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example based on units of group rings

paper.abstract:
The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers. For every $k\ge0$, the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers using rationals of $\Ind(\KG(3,k))$ are \[
  \beta_6=\binom{k+5}{7}+29\binom{k+6}{7}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \beta_9=\binom{k+6}{6}. \] The proof uses an inductive decomposition based on a simplicial retraction and Barmak's star clusters, Dowker duality together with Jonsson's computation of the homology of complexes of graphs with bounded covering number, and a relative Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence which reduces the problem to the six-element sets.
paper.title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples

paper.abstract: A finite free chain model for the homology of a Hausdorff ample groupoid \(G\) is cut out of the Matui complex by a finite clopen partition of each nerve space. We ask what such a model must supply and isolate three requirements: a single model that is a quasi-isomorphism, a chain of models that is a complete system with ranks and transition maps read off the presenting data, and a bound on the number of atoms in terms of the presenting cover. An \(n\)-Helly axiom on the presenting covers supplies none of them, being satisfied by every finite atomization for every \(n\), and a \(1\)-Helly family of \(N\) compact open sets can have \(2^{N}-1\) atoms. We show that a laminar presentation, a laminar basis of compact open sets in each nerve degree, supplies the third, and the second as soon as it is countable: the atoms of a finite laminar family are exactly its nonempty nodes, so a subordinate model has rank at most the number of members presenting it, the subordinate models of finite height form a complete system containing, for a countable presentation, a chain that is itself complete, and the transition maps are the least-ancestor maps of the presenting subfamilies. Every second countable Hausdorff ample groupoid admits one, and the choice is made in each nerve degree separately, laminarity not being stable under products. The first requirement is a restriction on \(G\): the homology of a model is finitely generated over a Noetherian ring, whereas \(H_0\) over \(\mathbb Z\) is not for the unit groupoid on a Cantor set or for the CAR groupoid, and a truncated model carries free homology of arbitrary rank in arbitrarily high odd degree where the groupoid has none. The chain-level statements are accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization.
paper.title: A Note on Laminar Presentations and Finite Chain Models for Ample Groupoid Homology

paper.abstract: In this note we study extension of standard Euclidean degree in nonlinear analysis to the setting of general oriented topological manifolds. The axiomatization of Euclidean degree is adapted to this setting. Existence and uniqueness are proven. The existence does not rely on smooth approximations as in the Euclidean case -- this is irrelevant for manifolds which do not admit a smooth structure and could be ambiguous for manifolds admitting many smooth structures. Rather, we rely on a cohomological approach using only topological information. When compared to the Euclidean case, we think this approach makes the proofs simpler and more transparent. The standard notion of a degree of maps between closed oriented manifolds studied in algebraic topology is recovered as a special case. A generalization of the notion of winding number is developed and related to the notion of degree. The familiar composition formula of the Euclidean degree is also obtained in this context.
paper.title: Axiomatic degree theory on topological manifolds

paper.abstract: We prove comparison results about $\infty$-categories of derived commutative rings with extra algebraic structure. For example, we show that several notions of derived $\delta$-rings agree and obtain similar results for derived $\lambda$-rings, derived binomial rings, and derived Boolean rings. Our comparison results apply more generally to modules over a specific kind of monad on derived rings that we call derived plethory.
paper.title: Derived plethystic algebra

paper.abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.
paper.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four

paper.abstract: A pair of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$ is a \emph{Fourier--Mukai (FM) pair} if there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories of derived sheaves of abelian groups \[\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))\simeq \operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z)).\] An FM pair $(X,Y)$ is \emph{non-trivial} if $X$ and $Y$ are not homeomorphic. We consider the question of whether non-trivial FM pairs $(X,Y)$ exist for which $X$ and $Y$ are both "nice" spaces, which in this article means admitting a triangulation. We show that the answer is no if $X$ is second-countable and either (i) one-dimensional, (ii) a surface, or (iii) the 3-sphere. In order to prove this, we define two invariants of dualizable categories. The first invariant is an extension of \emph{Tate--Hochschild cohomology} (aka singular Hochschild cohomology) to a class of dualizable categories satisfying a countability assumption. For a homology manifold $X$, we relate the Tate--Hochschild cohomology of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))$ to the homology at infinity of $X$ (in the sense of proper homotopy theory). The second invariant takes the form of a subcategory $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{Gor}}\subseteq\mathcal D$ called the \emph{Gorenstein locus}, defined for every dualizable stable category $\mathcal D$. For a triangularizable space $X$ and a field $k$, we show that the Gorenstein locus of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(k))$ is equal to the full subcategory of sheaves supported on the $k$-homology manifold locus of $X$.
paper.title: Reconstruction of graphs and surfaces from derived categories

paper.abstract:
The expressivity of a neural network $\Phi$ describes the class of functions that a network can express. The term topological expressivity refers to a family of measures particularly suited to understand binary classification and is often formulated in terms of the Betti numbers of a decision boundary $\beta (\Phi^{-1}(0))$. Despite its popularity, this measure is not as useful for regression and other problems that do not involve a decision boundary. Instead, we propose to study topological expressivity in terms of the Betti numbers of the output of a neural network $\beta(\Phi(X))$. We formally prove that a ReLU network with architecture $(d,\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d
  } \beta_k(3k+2),\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d}\beta_k(k+1))$ can express spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers. This gives upper bounds for any arbitrary connected ($\beta_0=1$) sequence of Betti numbers, but by constructing spaces homotopy equivalent to products of $N$ spheres of dimension $d_1,...,d_N$ we achieve much better bounds $(\sum\limits_{n=1} d_n, 3\sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + 2N, \sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + N) $ for Betti numbers given by $\prod_n (1+x^{d_n})$. Finally we conjecture a much stronger tight bound which gives the architectural bound $(d,d+1,d+1)$ for a space homeomorphic to the sphere.
paper.title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks

paper.abstract: We study the (typical) singularities of the distance function from a point in the ambient space to a polytopal complex in Euclidean space. By means of the Goresky-MacPherson splitting we generalize the existing linear theory to the quadratic distance function. Critical points occur on `selected' strata of the PL-space, where normal Morse Data determine the change of topology. On the homology level there exist indices with multiplicities, combined in a Morse vector. We focus mainly on PL-manifolds. We give bounds, depending on the dimension of the strata. In low dimensions we describe singularity types. At the end we discuss relations with Discrete Morse Theory.
paper.title: Critical Point Theory for the Distance Function on PL-Spaces

paper.abstract: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic \`a la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic \`a la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic \`a la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.
paper.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms

paper.abstract: We compute the first homology of the unordered configuration space of $n$ open unit-squares in the $w$ by $h$ rectangle for all positive integers $n$, $w$, and $h$. Letting $w$ and $h$ vary, these square configuration spaces form a bi-filtration of the unordered configuration space of $n$ points in the plane, so their fundamental groups approximate the $n$-strand braid group. Using a pair of spectral sequences, we prove that these square and point configuration spaces have naturally isomorphic first homology groups if $w,h\ge 3$ and $n\le wh-3$. In the $h=2$ case, we show that the first homology groups of these square configuration spaces are free of rank $n-1$ for $n\le 2w-2$, whereas they are free of rank $w-1$ for $n=2w-1$.
paper.title: The first homology of square-section braid groups

paper.abstract: We introduce weak $A_n$-formality for Galois cochain algebras and, for profinite groups whose mod-$p$ cohomology is concentrated in degrees at most two, characterise weak and genuine $A_n$-formality through finite embedding problems and the projective system they form. We then study $A_n$-formality for number fields. Let $K$ be a number field and let $p$ be an odd prime with $\mu_p\not\subset K$. For $p\geq 5$, and for $p=3$ under a natural local cyclotomic condition, we prove that every associated finite $A_3$-embedding problem is solvable. In contrast, for every odd $p$ with $\mu_p\not\subset K$, we show that no compatible family of finite-stage solutions exists, and hence $C^\bullet(G_K,\mathbb F_p)$ is not genuinely $A_3$-formal. The proof uses Chebotarev density, governing fields, and the Gras-Munnier criterion to obstruct the compatibility of finite-stage solutions, and it builds on previous work of Maire-Min\'a\v{c}-Ramakrishna-T\^an. This shows that genuine $A_3$-formality detects a global compatibility obstruction for number fields invisible to every individual finite embedding problem and invisible to obstructions arising from individual strong Massey vanishing problems.
paper.title: Weak and genuine A_n-formality for number fields

paper.abstract: We show that integers act invertibly on a derived scheme $S$ if and only if they act invertibly on the reduced motivic suspension spectrum of the affine line in $\mathrm{MS}_S$. As a consequence, over regular locally noetherian schemes and derived schemes on which some nonzero integer acts as zero, the motivic sphere spectrum is $\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant after inverting primes that are not invertible in the base scheme. In particular, over regular locally noetherian $\mathbf{Q}$-schemes, the motivic sphere spectrum is $\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant.
paper.title: Loyalty of the affine line in motivic homotopy theory

paper.abstract: We develop a semisimple obstruction theory for finite-length abelian categories. To each object \(X\) we associate a canonical obstruction subobject \(\mathcal O(X)\), consisting of the part invisible to all morphisms into semisimple objects. The quotient \(X/\mathcal O(X)\) is semisimple and universal among such morphisms, yielding a canonical semisimplification reflector and characterizing semisimplicity by the vanishing of obstruction. Iterating the construction gives an obstruction filtration which, in finite-length module categories, recovers the classical radical filtration and Loewy theory. Obstruction is also heart-dependent: under Happel--Reiten--Smal{\o} tilting, extension data can appear as new obstruction layers, leading to obstruction shadows and visible torsion. Thus classical radical theory arises as the fixed-heart module-theoretic instance of a categorical framework for semisimple reconstruction, persistence, and variation of heart.
paper.title: Universal Semisimple Reconstruction and Obstruction Theory

paper.abstract: In this paper, we study the tensor triangular geometry of band algebras $RB$, where $B$ is a finite left regular band and $R$ is a commutative Noetherian ring. We show that the Balmer spectrum of $\Perf(RB)$ is homeomorphic to $\Spec R\times L_B$, where $L_B$ is the support lattice of $B$. We also show that there is a bijection between the localizing ideals of $D(RB)$ and the stable subsets of $\Spec R\times L_B$. As a consequence, the telescope conjecture holds for $D(RB)$. Finally, we construct a band $B$ such that the generalized Nerves of Steel Conjecture fails for the non-rigid tensor triangulated category $\Perf(RB)$.
paper.title: Tensor triangular geometry of band algebras

paper.abstract: In this paper, we study the rational realization of the gap-two product $K(\Q,n)\times K(\Q,n+2)$ as the classifying space $\B(X)$ for a simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$ with rational homology of finite type. We prove that $K(\Q,n)\times K(\Q,n+2)$ can be realized as $\B(X)$ up to rational homotopy equivalence if and only if $n=3,4$ or $4m+2$ for $m\geq 1$. Moreover, we determine all their minimal Sullivan models up to isomorphism. The rational homotopy type of such $X$ is unique for $n=3$ or $4m+2$ for $m\geq 1$; there exist infinitely many rational homotopy types of such $X$ for $n=4$.
paper.title: A complete classification of the rational realization of gap-two products of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces as classifying spaces

paper.abstract: For $n\ge1$, we study representations of a simplicial group $G$ in the full $\infty$-subcategory of simplicial vector spaces whose normalized homology is concentrated in degrees $0,\ldots,n-1$, retaining its full mapping spaces. The resulting functor category depends only on the $n$-truncated homotopy type of $\mathbf{B}G$ and admits projectively bifibrant strict diagram and simplicial group-algebra module models. If restriction along a specified map $f:G\to H$ is an equivalence, then $\pi_0(f)$ is a group isomorphism; the proof uses ordinary extension and restriction of scalars. Yet for every $n\ge2$ and prime $q$ invertible in $k$, the nontrivial source $K(\mathbb Z/q,n-1)$ has the same $n$-representation category with vertex evaluation as the trivial group. The group-algebra augmentation is a weak equivalence, so the constant functor is also an equivalence for untruncated representations. Thus $n$-representations depend only on the $n$-truncation of $\mathbf{B}G$, but need not determine that truncation, even together with vertex evaluation.
paper.title: A Note on n-Representations of Simplicial Groups

paper.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed, smooth or topological $n$-manifold, with $n \geq 4$. We construct a homotopy highly cartesian square relating the space ${\mathcal E}(M (\ell))$ of homotopy self-equivalences of $M$ (in a suitable range) over the Postnikov $\ell$-sections of its stable normal microbundle, and an $(\infty + n)$-fold loop space representing an associated (normal) bordism theory. This implies the existence of braids of interlocking exact sequences involving the homotopy groups of ${\mathcal E}(M(\ell))$ and certain Lashof bordism groups, leading to a conceptual explanation and broad generalization of earlier work of Hambleton--Kreck for closed, oriented $4$-manifolds.
paper.title: Braidings of Self-Equivalences and Bordism

paper.abstract: We study several fundamental properties of the category $\mathbf{Kur}$ introduced in \cite{Kim1}. By defining fibrations and weak equivalences, we show that morphisms with manifold targets admit homotopy fiber products; this is then applied to obtain a notion of generalized intersections of two submanifolds. A definition of the Weinstein category in the context of Kuranishi spaces is also presented. Finally, we establish that $\mathbf{Kur}$ forms a category of fibrant objects in the sense of Brown \cite{Brown}, and discuss its homotopy category $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathbf{Kur})$.
paper.title: Kuranishi spaces in a category of fibrant objects and their homotopy fiber products

paper.abstract: Multiparameter complex processes, based on the Costa-Farber model, provide a common framework for growing random simplicial complexes, including the Linial-Meshulam and random flag complex processes. We establish laws of large numbers for persistent Betti numbers of these processes and prove that, after a deterministic time change and normalization, their persistence diagrams converge weakly in probability to a deterministic finite measure. Its quadrant masses are determined by universal limits of normalized persistent Betti numbers, characterized by an explicit finite-dimensional optimization problem. We extend the diagram convergence to integrals of continuous functions with polynomial growth in the death coordinate and controlled singularities at the diagonal. These results yield convergence of additive and multiplicative lifetime measures and total persistence. We further deduce convergence in optimal transport distance. The proofs combine local weak convergence of simplicial pairs, spectral analysis of compressed Laplacians accounting for dependence through shared faces, and quantitative estimates for large death coordinates and short lifetimes.
paper.title: Limit Theorems for Persistent Homology of Multiparameter Complex Processes

paper.abstract: We revisit the relation between the Kontsevich commutative graph complex and the homology of $\GL(n,\Z)$ found by Brown--Chan--Galatius--Payne using the sharbly complex of Ash--Miller--Patzt.
paper.title: The graph complex and the homology of the general linear groups revisited

paper.abstract: Let $f:(\C^n,0)\to(\C,0)$ be a holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point at the origin, and let $\varphi_f$ be the negative gradient flow of $\re f$ with respect to a Riemannian metric. We show that the origin is an isolated invariant set of $\varphi_f$ and that its Conley index is the suspension of the Milnor fiber, \[ h(\varphi_f,\{0\})\;\simeq\;\Sigma F_f\;\simeq\;\bigvee_{\mu(f)}S^n , \] so that $\mu(f)=\rank \CH_n(\varphi_f,\{0\};\Z)$: the Milnor number is the rank of the homological Conley index of the flow in degree $n$. The proof uses continuation to a holomorphic morsification of $f$. Since $\im f$ is a first integral of the flow, after a rotation of the target through an angle avoiding finitely many values there are no connecting orbits between the $\mu(f)$ nondegenerate rest points that result, and the sum property of the Conley index applies. McCord's theorem then recovers the Poincar\'e--Hopf index of $-\nabla\re f$.
paper.title: The Milnor Fiber as a Local Conley Index

paper.abstract: Let $A$ and $X$ be connected based CW complexes with $H_1(A;\mathbb Q)\neq 0$, and let $m\geq 1$ be the least degree with $\widetilde H_m(X;\mathbb Q)\neq0$. We prove that the Bousfield--Kan rational completion map of $A\vee X$ induces a map on $H_{2m}(-;\mathbb Q)$ whose cokernel has dimension at least $2^{\aleph_0}$. In particular, $A\vee X$ is $\mathbb Q$-bad.
paper.title: Wedges, Rational completion and $\mathbb Q$-bad spaces

paper.abstract: A Fourier–Mukai equivalence between smooth proper complex varieties of common even dimension preserves the topological signature. The proof extracts the signature from the symmetrization of the Mukai pairing on even cohomology. Combining this observation with known derived invariants and the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg decomposition shows that derived-equivalent smooth projective fourfolds over any field of characteristic zero have the same Hodge numbers. This argument and text was produced by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol.
paper.title: Derived invariance of the signature and Hodge numbers of fourfolds

paper.abstract: We construct finite free group schemes of rank four and exponent eight as stabilizers in a smooth two-dimensional affine group. We first compute the complete local deformation ring of the invariant space of constants and squares in characteristic two, using six Grassmannian coordinates. For every Artinian specialization, evaluation at the identity has a finite free rank-four stabilizer. Its fourth-power morphism is $(x,y)\mapsto(2bxy,2axy)$, and its eighth-power morphism is trivial. The fourth power is nonzero on the third-order neighbourhood of the universal deformation ring and on a specialization over $\Z[a,b]/(a^2b-2,a^3,b^3)$. We give complete formulas for the latter group scheme. Right translation preserves the chosen quadratic space exactly when it contains the square of the scalar character. This identifies $(2a,2b)$ as the common obstruction to fourth-power vanishing, normality of the stabilizer, and two-sidedness in an equivalent cyclic-module construction.
paper.title: Frobenius orbit maps and rank-four group schemes

paper.abstract: We deduce from Bhatt's graded Cohen--Macaulay and vanishing results that an integer-graded absolute integral closure of a weighted polynomial ring over $\Z_p$, modulo $p$, is free with basis degrees smaller than the sum of the weights. A direct $p$-adic expansion turns this degree bound into a uniform solution of the cusp relation modulo nilpotents. Consequently every ring $R$ admits a faithfully flat algebra with seminormal reduction, and every invertible $R[T]$-module becomes free after a faithfully flat extension of $R$, answering a question of Drinfeld.
paper.title: Graded absolute integral closures and Picard groups

paper.abstract: For every Hochschild diagonal of a smooth projective complex variety, a Fourier–Mukai equivalence preserves both the ordinary Hodge-number sum and the sum signed by the parity of the antiholomorphic degree. The latter is the signature of a Hermitian form obtained from the generalized Mukai pairing. In dimension five these invariants determine $h^{0,3}$ and $h^{1,4}$ and reduce the unrestricted Hodge-number problem to two numerical parameters, one of which is the possible failure of invariance of $h^{0,2}$. Albanese methods remove this structure-sheaf ambiguity when the Albanese image has dimension at least three. The general fivefold case remains open, while a theorem of Abuaf proves invariance of all Hodge numbers for fivefolds with trivial canonical bundle.
paper.title: Signed Mukai diagonals and derived equivalences of fivefolds

paper.abstract: We establish rational Swan induction for ordinary perfect modules over the finite-local sphere $L_n^{p,f}\mathbb S$. For a finite abelian ambient group, subgroups of $p$-rank at most $n+1$ suffice, and this bound is sharp. The proof combines cyclic homotopy fixed points in telescopic spectra with the isotropy filtration of a chromatic quotient of finite genuine spectra. The result proves Conjecture~7.22 of Clausen--Mathew--Naumann--Noel for Morava $E$-theory and gives a new proof of their chromatic upper bound for the algebraic $K$-theory of $L_n^{p,f}\mathbb S$-linear categories. The quotient argument also produces finite complexes realizing the induction relations. We formulate the problem of explicit realizations and give two geometric models at the prime two.
paper.title: Swan induction for the finite-local sphere

paper.abstract: For every odd prime $p$, we construct a regular strictly henselian local ring $A$ whose generic fibre has \'etale cohomology classes in $H^2_{\et}(A[1/p],\mu_p^{\otimes2})$ which are not sums of cup products of degree-one classes. The ring is the strict henselization of a local ring on a finite-type arithmetic scheme. A unit on a principal divisor gives an element of order $p$ in $SK_1(A[1/p])$, detected by its localization boundary on the special fibre. Adams--Riemann--Roch and the connectivity of the motivic filtration show that this element has nonzero image in $H^3_{\mot}(A[1/p],\Z(2))$. The integral coefficient sequence then gives the cohomological obstruction. Only the eigenvalues $4$ and $8$ of $\psi^2$ are needed.
paper.title: Torsion in $K_1$ and $p$-adic vanishing cycles

paper.abstract: We prove that for every odd prime $p$ there is a height $n$ for which the map $L_{n-1}S_p \to L_{n-1}\L_{K(n)}S_p$ is not injective on homotopy groups, hence not the inclusion of a wedge summand. In particular, for such pairs $(n,p)$ the weak chromatic splitting conjecture is false. More precisely, we prove the conjecture fails for $(n,p) = (3,3)$ and for all pairs $(n,p)$ with $p \le n < \sqrt{2}(p-1)$. In particular, the conjecture fails for $(n,p) = (p,p)$ for every odd prime $p$. This disproof was produced autonomously by Claude in a session working on Freyd's generating hypothesis with no human in the loop. This note is a human write-up of the disproof. We did not contribute any ideas.
paper.title: Weak chromatic splitting fails at n = p for every odd prime p

paper.abstract: We explain a Lean 4 formalization of the classical Seifert van Kampen theorem for the full fundamental groupoid. For an arbitrary topological space covered by two open subsets, the inclusion-induced square of ordinary continuous-path fundamental groupoids is a pushout in the category of categories. Every point is retained as an object; no basepoint, connectedness, or separation hypothesis is required. The development identifies an auxiliary directed path category for the indiscrete preorder with Mathlib's fundamental groupoid through strictly inverse functors and naturality equalities. It then assembles the pushout universal property from attributed path-subdivision and homotopy-grid helpers adapted from the directed-topology formalization of Basold, Bruin, and Lawson. We describe the descent construction, its transfer to ordinary fundamental groupoids, and the statement and verification boundaries of the exact artifact registered in Palomar. This is an expository account of a classical theorem and an existing formal artifact, with no claim of mathematical novelty or formalization priority.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz
paper.title: A Lean Formalization of the Classical Seifert van Kampen Groupoid Theorem

paper.abstract:
Let $E$ be a nonempty finite set. A shade map on $E$ is a map $T:\mathcal{P}(E)ightarrow\mathcal{P}(E)$ such that toggling an element $u
otin T(F)$ in the input $F$ does not change $T(F)$. We prove that, if $T$ is an inclusion-reversing shade map and $G\subseteq E$, then the simplicial complex \[ \{F\subseteq E\mid G\subseteq T(F)\} \] is collapsible. Equivalently, if $S$ is an inclusion-preserving shade map, then the Alexander dual of \[ \{F\subseteq E\mid G
ot \subseteq S(F)\} \] is collapsible. This is an Alexander-dual companion to the shade-map collapsibility theorem in \emph{The Elser nuclei sum revisited}. The proof first matches all faces on which $T(F)
eq E$ by a toggle. The remaining faces, characterized by $T(F)=E$, form the free convex set complex of an associated antimatroidal quasi-closure operator. We give a self-contained recursive acyclic matching on this complex. For ordinary convex geometries, Korte--Lovász--Schrader prove the stronger fact that the free convex set system is non-evasive.
paper.title: Collapsibility of Alexander duals for shade maps

paper.abstract: A systematic way to construct Poisson brackets on moduli stacks in algebraic geometry is through shifted Poisson structures on derived stacks. The standard construction, due to Calaque--Pantev--To{\"e}n--Vaqui{\'e}--Vezzosi, imports Gelfand--Kazhdan formal geometry to derived stacks in order to establish formal descent for polyvector fields. The result is a graded Lie algebra which we call the ``crystalline'' polyvector fields on a derived stack. Using instead the formal derived geometry machinery of Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum, we construct a graded Lie algebra of ``infinitesimal'' polyvector fields which has a direct geometric interpretation: it governs deformations of the formal shifted cotangent stack, together with its canonical exact symplectic form. Our main result is an equivalence between crystalline and infinitesimal polyvector fields on a derived stack as graded Lie algebra objects, providing a deformation-theoretic perspective on the graded Lie algebra constructed by Calaque--Pantev--To{\"e}n--Vaqui{\'e}--Vezzosi.
paper.title: Crystalline and infinitesimal Poisson stacks

paper.abstract: The finite-dimensional Pauli problem asks how many measurements in orthonormal bases determine every pure state of a \(d\)-level quantum system up to a global phase. Four bases always suffice, and the answer is known to be three for \(d=2\) and four for \(d=3\) and \(d\geq5\). Dimension four remained open because the embedding argument used in other dimensions fails there: the pure-state space \(\mathbb{CP}^3\) embeds in \(\R^9\), the space of the nine independent probabilities of three bases. We show that three bases do not suffice in \(\C^4\), so exactly four are needed. The same argument shows that no ten vectors in \(\C^4\) do phase retrieval. Since eleven vectors are known to suffice, the smallest phase-retrieval frame and the smallest rank-one POVM distinguishing all pure states in \(\C^4\) both have eleven elements. All three lower bounds follow from one statement: every six-dimensional real space of traceless Hermitian \(4\times4\) matrices with a common isotropic vector, that is, a nonzero \(e\) with \(e^*Te=0\) for all \(T\) in the space, contains a nonzero matrix of rank at most two. We prove it with complex \(K\)-theory: otherwise, an odd unitary map on the five-sphere would have a \(K^1\)-class that is nonzero by antipodal symmetry but vanishes because of the isotropic vector.
paper.title: Pauli problem in dimension 4

paper.abstract:
Let $H_n$ be the one-dimensional Honda formal group of height $n$ over $\mathbf F_{p^n}$ and let \[ R_n=W(\mathbf F_{p^n})[[u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}]],\qquad A_n=R_n/(p). \] We prove, for every height $n$ and every prime $p$, that the prime ideals of $A_n$ stable under an open subgroup of the Morava stabilizer group are exactly the height ideals $(u_1,\ldots,u_j)$. We also prove that a stable prime of $R_n$ avoiding $p$ is zero. The resulting radical-ideal classification implies the Hovey-Strickland classification of thick tensor ideals in the category of dualizable $K(n)$-local spectra via the forward implication of Barthel-Heard-Naumann.
  The special-fiber argument is local and geometric. After cutting an invariant prime by a one-parameter curve, we construct from the Cartier structure equation a smooth formal quotient $\mathcal{Q}$ and a distinguished subgroup $\mathcal{H}$. The generic fiber of $\mathcal{H}$ is identified with the deformation space of connected-\'etale extensions. A Cartier obstruction map from the full Honda endomorphism order is compared with evaluation on Tate vectors through completed universal covers. Fargues-Fontaine vector bundles give a period-detection statement. Chai's rigidity theorem then promotes detection by homomorphisms to formal Zariski density after a renormalization of the valuation. A uniform fixed-jet argument transfers this density to Morava-stabilizer orbits. The generic-fiber assertion is proved separately from the Gross-Hopkins period map.
paper.title: Invariant Primes in Lubin-Tate Space and Hovey-Strickland at Every Height

paper.abstract: We disprove the classical version of the Borsuk-Ulam-flavored conjecture, due to Baum-D{\k{a}}browski-Hajac, that free actions $X\times \mathbb{G}\to X$ on non-empty compact Hausdorff spaces by non-trivial compact groups admit no equivariant maps $X*\mathbb{G}\to X$. Specifically, among non-trivial compact abelian $\mathbb{G}$, the conjecture fails precisely when $\mathbb{G}$ is torsion-free profinite.
paper.title: Nullhomotopic equivariant shifts and Borsuk-Ulam-compatible compact abelian groups

paper.abstract: $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces are a class of oriented folded surfaces with a fundamental $H_2(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$ class. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces that embed in $3$-manifolds. This perspective naturally leads to the definition of the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Thurston norm, which generalises the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Thurston norm of Jaco, Rubinstein and Tillmann and adapts Turaev's definition of $\theta$. We define canonical $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces, which connect the theory of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces to the study of one-vertex $3$-manifold triangulations, and we relate their Euler characteristic to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Thurston norm. We generalise a classical result of Bredon and Wood by proving that the maximum Euler characteristic of a non-separating non-empty $\mathbb{Z}_3$-folded surface embedded in $L(3n,1)$ is $2-n$ for $n\in\mathbb{Z}^{>0}$, determining the $\mathbb{Z}_3$-Thurston norm in these cases. We conclude by demonstrating the motivating application of this theory to the study of generalised triangulations by proving that any generalised triangulation of the lens space $L(3n,1)$ must have at least $n$ tetrahedra. This final result is a preview of joint work with Spreer in which we determine the exact complexity of $L(3n,1)$ using more sophisticated techniques.
paper.title: $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces and the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Thurston norm

paper.abstract:
The computational complexity of simplicial homology has been studied since the question was raised by Kaibel and Pfetsch, and clique homology was later shown to be $\mathsf{QMA}_1$-hard by Crichigno and Kohler. King and Kohler subsequently introduced the weighted, spectrally gapped version considered here and developed a reduction intended to establish the same hardness result in this setting.
  We give a complete proof of the hard direction. The earlier King-Kohler argument contains a gap in the analysis of the nontrivially folded local gadgets, so the required topological and spectral properties have to be re-established on the clique complexes actually produced by the reduction. This is not a local repair of the published proof: the argument requires a new analysis of the local topology, the filtered cochain complexes, and the interaction of many overlapping gadgets.
  Our proof uses exact finite certificates for the local combinatorial data and relative homology to determine the effect of each gadget on the encoded qubit space. We then prove the finite-dimensional filtered-Hodge statement needed to recover the corresponding rank-one low-energy penalty and derive a quantitative global estimate that transfers the source-Hamiltonian promise gap to the final weighted Hodge Laplacian. Consequently, for fixed efficiently computable $k(n)$ and inverse-polynomial $\gamma(n)$, weighted gapped clique homology is $\mathsf{QMA}_1(\mathcal G)$-hard. The previously known $\mathsf{QMA}$-containment argument is logically independent of the gap and remains unaffected.
paper.title: A Complete Proof of $\mathsf{QMA}_1$-Hardness for Weighted Gapped Clique Homology

paper.abstract: In this note, for every topological colored nonsymmetric operad with CW spaces in each arity we construct a homotopy isomorphism with a CW homotopy operad (i.e. all higher homotopies are cellular with respect to the product structure and CW structure on cubes) not changing its objects. By using the two-sided bar construction, we rectify this to a homotopy isomorphism with a strict CW operad. This applies more generally to topological algebras over colored operads in sets. In the case of diagrams of finite CW complexes over finite posets, the resulting diagram consists of finite CW spaces enhancing the Quillen adjunction between simplicial sets and topological spaces. As a byproduct, we produce an embedding of topological homotopy algebras over operads into the presheaf category over the branch resolution for the category of $P$-trees generalizing the known case of topological operads.
paper.title: Cellular approximations for nonsymmetric homotopy operads

paper.abstract: Farrell and Jones showed that negatively curved manifolds in dimension $\geq 5$ are topologically rigid in the sense that homotopy equivalence implies homeomorphism. In the smooth category, the result does not hold even for hyperbolic manifolds, and there are negatively curved manifolds $N$ homotopy equivalent to a given hyperbolic manifold $M$ but not diffeomorphic. For complex hyperbolic manifolds, the analogous construction is demonstrated only in dimensions of the form $8n+2$. In this paper, we prove this result in many other dimensions. The main approach involves the use of $EO$-theory of complex projective spaces to construct suitable examples of exotic spheres. These theories may be viewed as a version of real $K$-theory, and are defined at each prime $p$. The computation also yields positive results about the existence of free smooth $S^1$ and $S^3$ actions on exotic spheres which do not bound parallelizable manifolds.
paper.title: Exotic structures on hyperbolic manifolds via the EO-theory of Projective Spaces

paper.abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}(G,A,\alpha)$ be a discrete 2-group, given as the {categorical} extension of an ordinary group $G$ by an abelian group $A$. We define principal $\mathcal{G}$-bundles over a manifold in terms of \v{C}ech data over a good open cover. In the case of the manifold $S^2$, we calculate this bicategory explicitly, and identify its 2-skeleton. We compare with the holonomy bicategory $\mathrm{Fun}(*/\!\!/ \pi_{\le 2}(S^2), * /\!\!/ \mathcal{G})$, and provide a concrete equivalence between the two.
paper.title: Flat principal 2-group bundles on $S^2$ and their holonomy

paper.abstract: We study the conjectural characteristic class analogue of the Hodge index theorem for singular complex algebraic varieties, formulated by Brasselet-Sch\"urmann-Yokura which expresses the Goresky-MacPherson homology $L$-classes in terms of suitable Hodge-theoretic $L$-classes, for quotient spaces $X/G$, where $G$ is a finite group and $X$ is a pure-dimensional complex projective variety. Assuming that an equivariant $K$-theoretical version of the conjecture holds for $X$, we show that the characteristic class conjecture holds for $X/G$. Without assuming the equivariant $K$-theoretical version, we show that the characteristic class conjecture holds for $X/G$, provided that it holds for all fixed point sets $X^g$ and that a suitable normally nonsingular inclusion assumption is satisfied. Our approach is to work in equivariant analytic $K$-homology and equivariant algebraic $G$-theory and to identify the corresponding localized classes. On the analytic side, we identify the Banagl-Zagier equivariant $L$-classes with localized Chern character of the equivariant $K$-homology class of the signature operator defined by Banagl-Leichtnam-Piazza. On the algebraic side, we compute the localization of the equivariant motivic Hodge-Chern class transformation of the intersection Hodge module.
paper.title: On the conjectural Hodge index theorem for finite quotient spaces of singular varieties

paper.abstract: We present a scalable method for computing persistence pairing graphs from large cubical filtrations and use it to test whether graph organization among persistent classes contains information beyond persistence intervals alone. The method cancels equal-value pairs before global reduction, constructs the compressed complex in streaming form, and recovers graph transitions from one persistence reduction through projected relations and triangular event solves. We apply the method to 119 signed distance volumes from the DRP-372 porous media collection for permeability prediction. Each 256-cubed volume induces more than 135 million cubical cells before contraction, whereas the median compressed complex contains 37,471 generators. In validation grouped by material family, adding persistence pairing graph descriptors improves prediction over persistence summaries under both Ridge regression and partial least squares regression. In the stricter experiment that holds out one source project at a time, Ridge retains a modest improvement over persistence alone, although additional benefit beyond geometry and persistence is not consistent across projects. Two null models show that the observed persistence and graph coupling and edge target organization are strongly nonrandom, but neither uniquely explains the predictive improvement; the useful signal appears to reside mainly in coarser graph and event organization. Spatial analyses likewise distinguish persistence magnitude from graph prominence and reveal nonlocal organization among algebraically related persistence events. These results show that persistence pairing graphs provide structurally informative summaries beyond the barcode while exposing domain dependence and representative sensitivity that motivate more invariant relational descriptors.
paper.title: Scalable persistence pairing graphs on scalar fields with an application to porous media

papers.abstract:
In this paper, we give complete classifications of the finite groups $G$ for which the constant Eilenberg--Mac Lane spectra $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ are Anderson self-dual up to a virtual representation shift, and we determine all such shifts. For both of these spectra, we determine the representation periodicity lattice for every finite group.
  As applications, we obtain $RO(G)$-graded universal coefficient theorems relating equivariant homology and cohomology, together with formulas for the Anderson duals of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$-modules. In the $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ self-dual cases, we identify the graded $\mathbb F_2$-linear dual of the coefficient ring $\pi_\star^G H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ with a representation shift of the ring as a module over itself. This gives perfect multiplication pairings and graded self-injectivity.
papers.title: On the Anderson Dual of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$

papers.abstract: We study $\mathbf{E}_n$-algebras with ramification in their $\pi_0$ and in particular show that the existence of ramification places strong limitations on their chromatic behavior. In particular, we show that $\pi_0$ of nonzero $K(1)$-local $\mathbf{E}_4$-$\mathrm{KU}$-algebras cannot have a map from the ring of integers in a ramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$, and we show that a $p$-complete $\mathbf{E}_2$-ring with a map from a perfectoid ring into its $\pi_0$ is an associative $\mathbf{Z}_p$-algebra.
papers.title: Ramification in $\mathbf{E}_{n}$-algebras

papers.abstract: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.
papers.title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories

papers.abstract: We define the higher Dehn invariant on the Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical variants of scissors congruence $K$-theory, and prove that it makes these spectra into comodules over the spectral Sah algebra. This allows us to make the first formulation of the conjecture that the higher volume and Dehn invariants are jointly injective.
papers.title: Higher Spherical Scissors Congruence II: Comodules

papers.abstract: We compare homological and homotopical epimorphisms of associative algebras in monoidal $\infty$-categories. Assume that geometric realizations and pushouts of associative algebras exist and that tensoring preserves geometric realizations. Then every homological epimorphism is homotopical. If, in addition, the ambient category is additive and tensoring preserves finite coproducts, the converse holds. This extends the result of Chuang and Lazarev for dg-algebras. In the symmetric monoidal setting, we discuss consequences for centers and commutative refinements, as well as applications to derived analytic geometry.
papers.title: Homological and homotopical epimorphisms in monoidal $\infty$-categories

papers.abstract: From the perspective of homological algebra, exact categories are interesting because they possess derived categories. Typically, an additive category admits many exact structures. If the original category is sufficiently nice (for example, quasi-abelian), a classification of exact structures can be given in terms of certain Serre subcategories in the category of contravariant functors. It turns out that the derived categories of different exact structures are functorially related. This work is concerned with sufficient conditions for the derived equivalence of different exact structures on certain categories.
papers.title: On derived equivalences of exact structures on the category of representations $k[x]/(x^n)$

papers.abstract: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets. As an application of this result, we construct a binormal, combinatorial, proto-abelian category of Kashiwara crystals associated to any root system. In the case that the proto-exact category is a category of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers, we show how to reconstruct our family via the language of algebraic geometry codes, in particular motivating an extension to arbitrary finite fields. We provide explicit computations of the dimension and minimum distance for select families of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers.
papers.title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories

papers.abstract: We recast the theory of power operations in chromatic height $1$ using higher semiadditivity. In particular, we show that if the height $1$ cyclotomic extension of a commutative algebra $R$ is Galois, then power operations on $R$-algebras are exactly $\delta$-ring operations. We also show that semiadditive power operations on chromatically localized algebraic $K$-theory agree with power operations defined using polynomial functoriality. As an application, we deduce that the map from the $K$-theory of a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear symmetric monoidal category to its $K(1)$-localization is a $\delta$-ring homomorphism on the level of underlying spaces. It is well known that operations on the $K$-theory of $\mathbb{Q}$-linear symmetric monoidal categories are $\lambda$-ring operations, and since $\delta$-rings are `$p$-typical' $\lambda$-rings, this is an instance of the redshift philosophy.
papers.title: Semiadditive Power Operations in Chromatic Height $1$

papers.abstract: For an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum $R$ of chromatic height $k$, the trace method and the chromatic redshift imply that $T^n$-fixed point of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $R$ has chromatic height at most $k+n$. In this paper, we compute these heights for $H\mathbb{F}_p$, $H\mathbb{Z}$ and the $p$-complete connective image-of-$J$ spectrum $j_p$ for all primes and $n\geq1$, which are exactly $n-1$, $n$ and $n+1$, respectively. Our method is based on properties of Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology over $\mathrm{MU}$.
